[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner column_margin="default" column_direction="default" column_direction_tablet="default" column_direction_phone="default" text_align="left" row_position="default" row_position_tablet="inherit" row_position_phone="inherit" overflow="visible" pointer_events="all"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_tablet="inherit" column_padding_phone="inherit" column_padding_position="all" column_element_direction_desktop="default" column_element_spacing="default" desktop_text_alignment="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_backdrop_filter="none" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" overflow="visible" gradient_direction="left_to_right" overlay_strength="0.3" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" animation_type="default" bg_image_animation="none" border_type="simple" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]WELCOMING ACTIVITY

Purpose: To help further develop communication skills by following an established protocol that engages students to share and discuss their responses to a text, quote, image, or video clip through the Save the Last Word activity. This strategy encourages everyone to be an active speaker, an active listener and supports equity of voice by ensuring that frequent speakers give space for others to share. Skills for Learning and Life Signature Practices Playbook (optional)

Skills for Learning and Life Focus: This Save the Last Word activity will further enhance students’ competencies of Self-Awareness, Self-Management, Social Awareness, and Relationship Skills.

Overview:

  1. Welcome students - lead a Community Circle/ Class Meetings activity, see (Optional)
    • Skills for Learning and Life Signature Practices Playbook 
    • Introduction to Welcoming Rituals
    • Greetings
  1. Identify culturally relevant reading passages, quotes, images, or video clips that will serve as the catalyst for students to discuss multiple bilingual career options.
  2. Have participants read/view the selected text/quote/image or video and highlight three sentences or make note of three ideas that particularly stand out for them.
  3. Ask participants to write each sentence/idea on the front of a sheet of paper or a 5x8 index card. On the back of the card, ask them to write 3-5 sentences explaining why they chose that quote or idea (what it meant to them, reminded them of, how it connects to their own experience, culture, language, history, etc.).
  4. Divide the students into groups of three, identifying one person as A, one person as B, and one person as C.
  5. Invite the A students to read one of their chosen quotations or ideas to their group. Then students B and C discuss the offering while student A listens. (For example, What do they think it means? Why do they think these words/ideas might be important in helping them identify multiple bilingual career options of interest? For whom?)
  6. After 1.5 minutes, ask student A to read the back of their card (or to explain why they picked the quotation or idea), thus having “the last word.”
  7. This process repeats with B sharing and others reflecting before B gets “the last word,” and then is repeated again with C sharing.
  8. Remind the students of LIA’s mission statement, “To empower youth through culture, service, leadership, and excellent education with the sole purpose of graduating from college.” Make sure that it is posted in a visible location.

 Debrief (3 min): (Reflection Model, Rolfe, 2001)

  1. What? What were your thoughts and feelings as you participated in this activity? (Self-Awareness)
  2. So What? Why do you think it’s important to be able to communicate ideas and opinions effectively and to be able to listen effectively? (Social Awareness) 
  3. Now What? What will you do with what you learned about multiple bilingual career options? (Responsible Decision Making)

 

Current Event Bell Starter

Relevancy/Linkage

  • Watch 2.02 Video Bilingual Advantage (3 min) and 2.02 Video Bilingual Cat (30 sec).
  • Discuss the following questions:
    • How does being bilingual give you an advantageous future?
    • How can languages be an asset to you in your future career?

Model

  • Tell the students the following:
    • Some students know exactly what they want to do for a career while others have no idea. Regardless of your situation, today we are going to explore additional options by researching bilingual career opportunities.
  • Model the research activity. Display 2.02 Bilingual Career Exploration Teacher Model. Read through each box, pausing to explain and elaborate. 
  • Invite the class to choose an additional career option and complete the corresponding questions as a class using 2.02 Weblink Bilingual Career Options and 2.02 Weblink Career Explorer.

Guided Practice

  • Distribute 2.02 HO Bilingual Career Exploration to each student. Provide students with the following links to research careers they are interested in or curious about:
    • 2.02 Weblink Bilingual Career Options 
    • 2.02 Weblink Career Explorer
  • For students who aren't sure about what career they want to pursue, provide the links below so they can take a survey before moving on to the research project:
    • 2.02 Weblink Career Options Survey (Spanish)
    • 2.02 Weblink Career Options Survey (English)

Independent Practice

  • Allow students time to explore additional bilingual career options.
  • Invite students to choose their top career choice and set a career goal using the 2.01 HO SMARTE Goal Template

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner column_margin="default" column_direction="default" column_direction_tablet="default" column_direction_phone="default" text_align="left" row_position="default" row_position_tablet="inherit" row_position_phone="inherit" overflow="visible" pointer_events="all"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_tablet="inherit" column_padding_phone="inherit" column_padding_position="all" column_element_direction_desktop="default" column_element_spacing="default" desktop_text_alignment="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_backdrop_filter="none" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" overflow="visible" gradient_direction="left_to_right" overlay_strength="0.3" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" animation_type="default" bg_image_animation="none" border_type="simple" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]Differentiation Idea – Option 1

  • Organize a Virtual Career Day where students can interact with local professionals to practice authentic academic conversations and experience extracurricular learning. Assign students to contact/recruit local experts to participate in a wide variety of careers by utilizing a Google Form to register and to receive instructions on how to virtually participate and/or record and submit their videos. Utilize Google Meet or Zoom to engage students in a live interactive session or have professionals create pre-recorded videos using Padlet to introduce themselves and to share details about their jobs. The interviews should ensure ethnic and linguistic diversity in connecting students with professionals that they can personally identify with.

Differentiation Idea – Option 2

  • Watch 2.02 Video Bilingual Benefits and ask students to listen for the following words and write possible definitions by using context clues: 
    • Evidence
    • Skills
    • Capture
    • Monitor
    • Executive
  • Discuss the results of the study.
  • Invite the students to create and/or take a Mock Stroop Test.

Differentiation Idea – Option 3

  • Introduce students to higher-paying technical career paths or career paths that accentuate their natural abilities. Encourage students to dream and assist them in finding an affordable, realistic way of reaching their career path.

Extension

  • Watch career exploration videos at https://roadtripnation.com/ and https://www.careeronestop.org/ExploreCareers/Assessments/interests.aspx.
  • Invite the student to take an online English and Spanish proficiency test.
    • 2.02 Weblink English Proficiency Test
    • 2.02 Weblink Spanish Proficiency Test
  • Discuss ways to improve grammar, vocabulary, and reading comprehension.
  • Allow the students time to create SMARTE language goals using 2.01 HO SMARTE Goal Template.

Journal Entry Suggestions

  • Students can add to their journals what they've learned about themselves, discuss the occupations they explored and found interesting, and ask any questions they still have about career planning.
  • Students can create video journals to document their personal growth, self-reflect, and share their thoughts and experiences. All major Learning Management Systems (LMS) support student recordings within the interface such as Screencastify Submit with Google Classroom or Canvas.
  • How have my bilingual skills helped me?
  • Share your goals to improve grammar, vocabulary, and reading comprehension.

  •  name positive attributes, activities or tasks that one can do well (Self-Awareness)

  • identify goals, wishes or dreams (Self-Management)

Purpose: To strengthen listening skills and encourage everyone to participate in a discussion through the Fishbowl activity. This activity can be used during a lesson to discuss content, or at the end of an engagement activity to give airtime to everyone about what they learned or found useful. Skills for Learning and Life Signature Practices Playbook (optional)

Skills for Learning and Life Focus: This Fishbowl activity will further enhance students' competencies of Self-Awareness, Self-Management, and Relationship Skills.

Overview:

  1. Welcome students - lead a Community Circle/ Class Meetings activity, see (Optional)
    • Skills for Learning and Life Signature Practices Playbook 
    • Introduction to Welcoming Rituals
    • Greetings
  1. In this Fishbowl activity, students are divided into two groups that are arranged in concentric circles, facing the center. The outside circle listens while the inside group has a discussion about career exploration. Then the groups switch places so the listeners become the speakers and vice versa. 
  2. Make sure the students know you will hold them accountable for sharing their observations. Use equity sticks (a cup of sticks with each student’s name on one) to increase participation and accountability.)
  3. Provide one question prompt related to career exploration. Here are a few examples (feel free to consider other questions): 
  • Name a few examples of personal goals.
  • What are some skills you will need to develop in order to reach your personal goals?
  • Name a few examples of professional/career goals you have considered.
  • What are some skills you will need to develop in order to reach your professional/career goals?
  1. Only the inside group members may speak during this time (4 minutes). Instruct the outside group to quietly listen and notice their own ideas that surface during the discussion. Note-taking on a graphic organizer may be helpful.
  2. When the time is up, ask the groups to trade places so that the outside group is sitting on the inner circle chairs and vice versa. Set the timer again for four minutes and let the new inside group discuss the topic.
  3. Remind the students of LIA’s mission statement, “To empower youth through culture, service, leadership, and excellent education with the sole purpose of graduating from college.” Make sure that it is posted in a visible location.

Debrief (3 min): (Reflection Model, Rolfe, 2001)

  1. What? What were your thoughts and feelings as you participated in this activity? (Self-Awareness)
  2. So What? Why do you think it’s important to explore your feelings about personal and professional/career goals? (Self-Management) 
  3. Now What? What will you do with what you learned today about exploring personal and professional/career goals? (Responsible Decision Making)

Current Event Bell Starter

Relevancy/Linkage

  • Review the previous lesson.
    • Say: Last time we explored bilingual career options.  Today we are going to explore what majors are offered and which major best fits your career interest.
  • Complete 2.03 Tupperware Activity Description and then ask the students the following questions:
    • Did all the lids fit all the Tupperware?
    • Did some lids fit more than one Tupperware?
    • How does this relate to choosing a major and a career?

  • Model
    • Explain: Many students choose a major they are interested in and then discover they dislike the career path.
    • Example: A student enjoys studying and learning about anatomy so the student chooses to study nursing. The student later finds out they do not like the sight of real blood or working directly with people.
    • Today we are going to explore what college majors are offered and what jobs those majors qualify you to do.
    • Display and use 2.03 Weblink Majors and 2.03 Career and Major Options Teacher Model to explain the first two education examples.

    Guided Practice

    • Distribute 2.03 HO Career and Major Options to each student.
    • Divide students into groups of 3 or 4 and allow each group to choose a major category of interest to research.  Groups preferably should choose a different category/major than other groups.
    • Allow student groups time to research their chosen categories.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner column_margin="default" column_direction="default" column_direction_tablet="default" column_direction_phone="default" text_align="left" row_position="default" row_position_tablet="inherit" row_position_phone="inherit" overflow="visible" pointer_events="all"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_tablet="inherit" column_padding_phone="inherit" column_padding_position="all" column_element_direction_desktop="default" column_element_spacing="default" desktop_text_alignment="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_backdrop_filter="none" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" overflow="visible" gradient_direction="left_to_right" overlay_strength="0.3" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" animation_type="default" bg_image_animation="none" border_type="simple" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text]Differentiation Ideas - option 1

  • Students work in pairs to identify and share personal strengths and interests and correlate how these qualities might impact their career paths. Students will pose the question: “What is Your Dream Job?” Students can interview their partner and share their partner’s information with the class. Provide a conversation sentence starter such as “My partner’s dream job is _______ because _________.”

This practice will foster oral language development and support ELs by re-envisioning pair and group work to support speaking and listening skills in English and their home language. When you hold students accountable, they know they must partner share, and listen to what their partner is saying. Students can record their partner’s responses on a voice recording app, such as Audacity, to support learning and remembering before presenting.

Differentiation Ideas - option 2

  • Broaden the major search to include certificate programs, technical schools, or other post-secondary options that best fit the students’ skill set and needs.

Extension

  • Have each group create a visual to display their results (e.g., poster or PowerPoint).

Journal Entry Suggestions

  • Where do I want to go now? What steps do I need to take to get there?
  • Students can create video journals to document their personal growth, self-reflect, and share their thoughts and experiences. All major Learning Management Systems (LMS) support student recordings within the interface such as Screencastify Submit with Google Classroom or Canvas.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner column_margin="default" column_direction="default" column_direction_tablet="default" column_direction_phone="default" text_align="left" row_position="default" row_position_tablet="inherit" row_position_phone="inherit" overflow="visible" pointer_events="all"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_tablet="inherit" column_padding_phone="inherit" column_padding_position="all" column_element_direction_desktop="default" column_element_spacing="default" desktop_text_alignment="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_backdrop_filter="none" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" overflow="visible" gradient_direction="left_to_right" overlay_strength="0.3" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" animation_type="default" bg_image_animation="none" border_type="simple" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text]WELCOMING ACTIVITYPurpose: To facilitate student interaction through the use of the Clock Buddies (Part 1) tool so that students will have specific partners for various activities throughout the period or week. This is a quick and easy way to create pairs for future partnered activities that offers a break from continually turning to an elbow partner. 

Skills for Learning and Life Focus: Interacting with Clock Buddies will further enhance students’ competencies of Self-Awareness, Relationship Skills, and Self-Management.

       Overview:

  1. Welcome students - lead a Community Circle/ Class Meetings activity, see (Optional)
    • Skills for Learning and Life Signature Practices Playbook 
    • Introduction to Welcoming Rituals
    • Greetings
  1. Dedicate time in your Community Circles/ Class Meetings to establish norms of collaboration on:
    1. how to greet each other once they meet their new Clock Buddy, 
    2. have them practice pronouncing each other's first and last names properly, 
    3. how they will ensure that each partner has equal time, and 
    4. how to thank each other once they have completed their activity instead of just walking away once the time is up. 
  2. Make copies of the Clock Buddy handout and distribute it to each student and ask them to write their own name at the top of their paper.
  3. Model how students should proceed in finding Clock Buddy partners by adding their names on the same time slot. Check to see if students understand the procedure. Make sure that they select someone who they are not familiar with or from a different country of origin.
  4. Have them continue finding Clock Buddies at a common time until all four time slots are filled. Invite students to return to their seats when the form is completed.
  5. Each time you need students to form pairs during the activity, have them take out their Clock Buddies sheet and announce one of the times for them to meet up with their Clock Buddy for this activity. For example, “Now meet up with your 9:00 Buddy to reflect and discuss..." Do this as a practice exercise.
  6. Use the Clock Buddies for the following activity: Write each of the following questions or activities on a separate 5x8 index card and spread them face down on a table or on the floor in the center of the Community Circle/Class Meeting. Have a student select a card and read it to the rest of the class (post on a whiteboard or PPT if possible). If it’s a question, give the students 1 minute to write a response in their journals before calling out which Clock Buddy they will meet with. Otherwise, they can engage immediately in the activity. The prompts for this activity could be (feel free to consider other questions or activities as well):
    1. Sit with your back against your buddy’s back on the floor and try to stand up together without using your hands.
    2. Make up a silly handshake with your buddy.
    3. Choose a classroom object with your buddy and write a short poem or rhyme about it.
    4. If one of your personal strengths was a superpower, what would it be? Explain what you would do with it to benefit others.
    5. Describe three skills or areas that you would like to improve. Why are they important to you?
    6. What does being successful mean to you? What do you use to measure progress? Success?
  7. Call out which Clock Buddy they will meet with to either share their response to the first question or begin the activity, i.e., meet with your 3:00 Buddy, etc. Repeat the process with a different question or activity for a few more Clock Buddy times (no more than 2 minutes for each Clock Buddy round). If time allows, select a few participants to share out after each round. 
  8. You can also use Clock Buddies for a Current Event Bell Starter, Guided Practice, Google My Maps Activity, Review and Assessment, and Adaptations.
  9. Remind the students of LIA’s mission statement, “To empower Latino youth through culture, service, leadership, and excellent education with the sole purpose of graduating from college.” Make sure that it is posted in a visible location.

Debrief (3 min): (Reflection Model, Rolfe, 2001)

  1. What? What were your thoughts and feelings as you signed up with your Clock Buddies? (Self-Awareness)
  2. So What? Why do you think it’s important to get to know other students who you do not know very well or are from a different country of origin? (Social Awareness) 
  3. Now What? What will you do with what you learned about working with others, your own superpowers, and personal strengths? (Relationship Skills and Self-Awareness)

Current Event Bell StarterRelevancy/Linkage

    • Review the previous lesson.
      • Last time we explored different major options available in groups and as a class.  Today you will have time to research your top three major and career choices individually.

  • Allow each student time to complete the handout.

  • Invite recent alumni to speak with students about their experiences in college, career training, or current employment. Utilize Google Meet or Zoom to engage students in a live interactive session. The interviews should ensure ethnic and linguistic diversity in connecting students with alumni that they can personally identify with. Students can prepare questions prior to the session. Some sample questions are:
    • What was the biggest transition from high school to college or work?
    • How did your time in high school help to prepare/impact you for your current career or college?
    • Why did you choose the college you are attending?
    • Did you know what you wanted to study in college?

Differentiation Ideas - Option 2

  • Use 2.04 HO Top 3 Major and Career Options (Spanish) version.

Extension

  • Invite the students to complete 2.04 Weblink Assessments for their second and third career options. 
  • Invite the students to search and complete other career/major assessments using another similar website.
  • Invite the students to write a short paragraph about their results expounding upon why they either agree or disagree with the results.

Journal Entry Suggestions

  • What careers interest me? What interests me about those careers?
  • What do I see myself doing in 10 years?
  • Students can create video journals to document their personal growth, self-reflect, and share their thoughts and experiences. All major Learning Management Systems (LMS) support student recordings within the interface such as Screencastify Submit with Google Classroom or Canvas.

Students should complete the SMARTE Goal Template that lists three SMARTE goals.

  • Two goals should be centered around the LIA standards.
  • One goal should be related to post secondary education.
  • All goals should reflect the characteristics of a SMARTE goal.

Students keep a copy of their goals worksheet in their paper or online portfolio.

OBJECTIVES:

Students will: 

  • complete an ACT and SAT overview and learn the value of both tests to post-secondary education.
  • understand that effort and practice help build confidence and that feeling confident helps you do your best and makes you proud (Self-Awareness) 
  • develop skills in planning and organizational skills (Self-Management)
  • demonstrate positive behaviors and self-regulation skills such as organization, completing tasks independently, bringing materials needed, planning projects, and making corrections (Self-Management)
  • appropriately asks for help or seeks support when needed (Relationship Skills)

Purpose: To build community by encouraging participants to interact with each other with the expectation that everyone's personal and professional goals are valued and are continuously evolving. The Mix and Mingle activity will have students move around the room and share ideas with a partner or small group.  See an example of the Mix and Mingle activity in the Skills for Learning and Life Signature Practices Playbook. (0ptional)

Skills for Learning and Life Focus: This Mix and Mingle activity will further enhance students’ competencies of Self-Awareness and Social Awareness.

Overview: 

  1. Welcome students - lead a Community Circle/ Class Meeting activity, see (Optional)
    • Skills for Learning and Life Signature Practices Playbook
    • Introduction to Welcoming Rituals
    • Greetings
  1. On a 5x8 card or half-sheet of paper, ask participants to write down a response to two prompts you give related to their own personal and professional goals: 
    1. How would you describe your own personal goals as they relate to your health, happiness, and a better lifestyle?
    2. How would you describe your own professional goals as they relate to success, financial stability, and job stability?
  2. Begin the "Mix and Mingle!" activity by turning on music so that the students can begin to move around the room (use samples of culturally familiar music such as cumbias, salsa, merengue, bachata, Norteños, mariachi, reggaeton, etc) 
  3. When the music stops, students need to find a partner near them. Help with pairing if needed.
  4. Partners share their responses on the cards, listen actively to each other, and ask follow-up questions for a total of 2 minutes.
  5. Start the music again and repeat the sequence a few more times with another partner, as your time permits.
  6. Remind the students of LIA’s mission statement, “To empower Latino youth through culture, service, leadership, and excellent education with the sole purpose of graduating from college.”

Debrief (3 min): (Reflection Model, Rolfe, 2001)

  1. What? What were your thoughts and feelings as you participated in this activity? (Self-Awareness)
  2. So What? Why do you think it’s important to explore and share your own personal and professional goals? (Social Awareness) 
  3. Now What? What will you do with what you learned about other people’s personal and professional goals? (Self Management)

Current Event Bell Starter

Relevancy/Linkage

*Teacher note: be sure to familiarize yourself with the ACT and SAT before teaching this lesson so that you have the most current information to share.

  • Ask the students the following questions:
  • What is the ACT? (American College Test)
  • What is the SAT? (Scholastic Aptitude Test)
  • How does the ACT differ from the SAT? How are they similar?
  • Why are these tests such a big deal?

  • Refer the students to 3.01 Weblink English-Spanish Post Secondary Glossary if they are unfamiliar with terms in the unit.
  • Use 3.01 HO ACT/SAT Online Resource Overview to find multi-level ACT/SAT study aids.
  • Inform students of fee waiver options by directing them to 3.01 Weblink SAT Fee Waiver or 3.01 Weblink ACT Fee Waiver

Extension

  • Inform students of the SAT and ACT testing accommodations available for English learners. Students may be able to take advantage of these testing accommodations and receive extra support for these assessments. Refer the students to the requirements for requesting accommodations at  https://satsuite.collegeboard.org/k12-educators/administration/sat-school-day/ordering/english-learner-supports and https://www.act.org/content/act/en/products-and-services/the-act/registration/accommodations.html. 

College Board offers testing supports for English learners (EL), including these:

  • Translated test directions - Directions are available in 15 languages.
  • Use of bilingual word-to-word dictionaries - The bilingual word-to-word dictionaries students use on test day must be from the College Board’s approved list.
  • 50% extended testing time – Test time may be extended to four-and-a-half hours instead of three. 

ACT Test Accommodations and English Learner Supports:

  • Extended time, not to exceed time and a half
  • Approved word-to-word bilingual dictionary (no definitions)
  • Test directions in the native language
  • Testing in a familiar environment/small group
  • Invite students to register for the ACT or SAT using 3.01 Weblink ACT Registration or 3.01 Weblink SAT Registration.
  • Research local university admission requirements. What minimum ACT or SAT score is required for admission and/or scholarships?
  • Ask students about their progress towards graduation. Have individual discussions with students or invite them to complete and turn in 3.01 HO Graduation Progress and Counselor Meeting (English) or 3.01 HO Graduation Progress and Counselor Meeting (Spanish). Having multiple copies of your high school registration booklet is suggested. Please modify the handout to fit the needs of your class. Review student information and selected options. Give encouragement and/or guidance to each student individually.

Journal Entry Suggestions

  • What can I do to be prepared for the ACT and SAT?
  • Students can create video journals to document their personal growth, self-reflect, and share their thoughts and experiences. All major Learning Management Systems (LMS) support student recordings within the interface such as Screencastify Submit with Google Classroom or Canvas.

OBJECTIVES:

Students will: 

  • take the English portion of the ACT or SAT practice test
  • understand that effort and practice help build confidence and that feeling confident helps you do your best and makes you proud (Self-Awareness)
  • understand the impact of developing self-discipline and self-motivation (Self-Management) 
  • demonstrate appropriate social behaviors to improve success, i.e., ask permission, ask for help, offer help to others, and contribute to the community. (Self-Management)
  • recognize the importance of effort in goal attainment (Self-Management)

INTRODUCTION

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner column_margin="default" column_direction="default" column_direction_tablet="default" column_direction_phone="default" text_align="left" row_position="default" row_position_tablet="inherit" row_position_phone="inherit" overflow="visible" pointer_events="all"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_tablet="inherit" column_padding_phone="inherit" column_padding_position="all" column_element_direction_desktop="default" column_element_spacing="default" desktop_text_alignment="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_backdrop_filter="none" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" overflow="visible" gradient_direction="left_to_right" overlay_strength="0.3" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" animation_type="default" bg_image_animation="none" border_type="simple" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text]WELCOMING ACTIVITY

Purpose: To facilitate and encourage student interaction through the use of the Clock Buddies (Part 1) tool so that students will have specific partners to discuss their strategies and better prepare for the ACT or SAT English Practice Test. This is a quick and easy way to create pairs for the rest of the partnered activities related to the other practice tests. 

Skills for Learning and Life Focus: Interacting with Clock Buddies will further enhance students’ competencies of Self-Awareness, Relationship Skills, and Self-Management.

Overview:

  1. Welcome students - lead a Community Circle/ Class Meeting activity, see (Optional)
    • Skills for Learning and Life Signature Practices Playbook
    • Introduction to Welcoming Rituals
    • Greetings
  1. Dedicate time in your Community Circles/ Class Meetings to establish norms of collaboration on:
    1. how to greet each other once they meet their new Clock Buddy, 
    2. have them practice pronouncing each other's first and last names properly, 
    3. how they will ensure that each partner has equal time, and 
    4. how to thank each other once they have completed their activity instead of just walking away once the time is up. 
  2. Make copies of the Clock Buddy handout and distribute it to each student and ask them to write their own name at the top of their paper.
  3. Model how students should proceed in finding Clock Buddy partners by adding their names on the same time slot. Check to see if students understand the procedure. Make sure that they select someone who they are not familiar with or from a different country of origin.
  4. Have them continue finding Clock Buddies at a common time until all four time slots are filled. Invite students to return to their seats when the form is completed.
  5. Use the Clock Buddies sheet each time you need participants to form pairs during an activity. For example, “Now meet up with your 9:00 Buddy to reflect and discuss..." Do this as a practice exercise.
  6. On a 5x8 card or a sheet of paper, ask participants to write down a response to a prompt you give related to their own strategies in taking the English portion of the ACT or SAT Practice Test. For example:
    1. Name three steps you can take to better prepare for the English practice test.
    2. Which areas in English do you feel more confident that you will do well on the test? Which areas do you feel the least prepared for (i.e., vocabulary, reading comprehension, writing, etc.)?
    3. What steps will you take to improve on your areas of greatest need?
  7. Call out a Clock Buddy time so that they can begin sharing their response to the questions (i.e., “Meet with your 3:00 Buddy!”, etc.). Repeat the process with a new Clock Buddy (no more than 2 minutes for each Clock Buddy round). 
  8. Once done, return to the community circle and invite a few students to share their responses and something they learned from their partners. 
  9. Have students turn in their Clock Buddies sheets before the end of the period and redistribute them the following day so that they can use them for additional partner activities.
  10. Remind the students of LIA’s mission statement, “To empower Latino youth through culture, service, leadership, and excellent education with the sole purpose of graduating from college.” Make sure that it is posted in a visible location.

  

 Debrief (3 min): (Reflection Model, Rolfe, 2001)

  • What? What were your thoughts and feelings as you signed up your Clock Buddies? (Self-Awareness)
  1. So What? Why do you think it’s important to get to know how other students will be preparing for the ACT or SAT Practice Test? (Social Awareness)
  2. Now What? What will you do with what you learned about strategies to prepare for the ACT or SAT Practice Test? (Relationship Skills and Self-Awareness)

Current Event Bell Starter

Relevancy/Linkage

  • Review the previous lesson.
  • Last time we looked at ACT and SAT similarities and differences to see which test is the best fit for you. Now that you have decided which test you are going to take, you will have time over the next four sessions to practice sections of your chosen test.

  • Go to 3.02 Weblink Practice Test or another free ACT/SAT practice test website. Note: When signing in with mac & using the safari browser, you must enable pop-ups by going to settings in Safari preferences.  Click on Security and uncheck “Block pop-up windows”.  Then click on privacy.  Locate “Block cookies and other website data” and select “never” from the list.
  • Show the students how to create an account and log in. Encourage the students to write down their login information.
  • Go to “My Account”, “Courses” then go to the “College Prep” tab and choose either the ACT or SAT practice tests.
  • Choose English for ACT or Writing for SAT
  • Note: If teachers create an account as well and give the students your ID and last name they can click on  “Add Monitor”, which will allow you to view their test progress and results.

Independent Practice

  • Allow students as much time as possible to take the English or Writing portion of their chosen test.

  • Create an online SAT or ACT practice test of the most common wrong answers noted on the ENGLISH practice test. Google forms or online polling applications, such as Mentimeter, Kahoot!, Socrative, or Quizziz, provide insight into levels of understanding and inform instruction to better meet the needs of English Learners. Students can effectively review missed questions by identifying the type of question, determining the strategy, and internalizing the concepts.  
  • Ask the students to take a screenshot to print or email results, if they did not add the teacher as a monitor.
  • Assist students in finding explanations to questions they missed or do not understand.

  • This is an alternative test prep website (can be used as a guest or by creating an account). Students may find this site more helpful and interactive.
  • 3.02 Weblink ACT Test Prep
  • Allow students to take other postsecondary entrance exams, such as the ASVAB or other technical school entrance exams.
  • Please consider this lesson as optional if there is minimal time to administer and review the practice test.

Extension

  • Allow students time to review their correct and incorrect answers.
  • Pair students in groups of 2 or 3, and have the students teach a concept or problem that they answered incorrectly.
  • Use other resources to help students prepare for the ACT/SAT test. See 3.01 ACT/SAT Resource Overview Page.

Journal Entry Suggestions

  • How can I prepare for the ACT/SAT? When am I planning on taking the ACT/SAT?
  • Students can create video journals to document their personal growth, self-reflect, and share their thoughts and experiences. All major Learning Management Systems (LMS) support student recordings within the interface such as Screencastify Submit with Google Classroom or Canvas.

OBJECTIVES:

Students will: 

  • take the math portion of the ACT or SAT practice test.
  • understand that effort and practice help build confidence and that feeling confident helps you do your best and makes you proud (Self-Awareness)
  • Understand the impact of developing self-discipline and self-motivation (Self-Management) 
  • demonstrate appropriate social behaviors to improve success, i.e., ask permission, ask for help, offer help to others, and contribute to the community. (Self-Management)
  • recognize the importance of effort in goal attainment (Self-Management)

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner column_margin="default" column_direction="default" column_direction_tablet="default" column_direction_phone="default" text_align="left" row_position="default" row_position_tablet="inherit" row_position_phone="inherit" overflow="visible" pointer_events="all"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_tablet="inherit" column_padding_phone="inherit" column_padding_position="all" column_element_direction_desktop="default" column_element_spacing="default" desktop_text_alignment="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_backdrop_filter="none" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" overflow="visible" gradient_direction="left_to_right" overlay_strength="0.3" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" animation_type="default" bg_image_animation="none" border_type="simple" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text]WELCOMING ACTIVITY

Purpose: To facilitate and encourage student interaction through the use of the Clock Buddies (Part 2) tool so that students will have specific partners to discuss their strategies and better prepare for the ACT or SAT Math Practice Test. This is a quick and easy way to create pairs for the rest of the partnered activities related to the other practice tests. 

Skills for Learning and Life Focus: Interacting with Clock Buddies will further enhance students’ competencies of Self-Awareness, Relationship Skills, and Self-Management.

Overview:

  1. Welcome students - lead a Community Circle/ Class Meeting activity, see (Optional)
    • Skills for Learning and Life Signature Practices Playbook
    • Introduction to Welcoming Rituals
    • Greetings
  1. Dedicate time in your Community Circles/ Class Meetings to establish norms of collaboration on:
    1. how to greet each other once they meet their new Clock Buddy, 
    2. have them practice pronouncing each other's first and last names properly, 
    3. how they will ensure that each partner has equal time, and 
    4. how to thank each other once they have completed their activity instead of just walking away once the time is up. 
  2. Make copies of the Clock Buddy handout and distribute it to each student and ask them to write their own name at the top of their paper. Follow the procedures for HS Lesson 3.02.
  3. On a 5x8 card or a sheet of paper, ask students to write down a response to a prompt you give related to their own strategies in taking the Math portion of the ACT or SAT Practice Test. For example:
    1. Name three steps you can take to better prepare for the Math Practice Test.
    2. Which areas in Math do you feel more confident that you will do well on the test? Which areas do you feel the least prepared in (i.e., basic operations, geometry, algebra, word problems, etc.)?
    3. What steps will you take to improve on your areas of greatest need?
  4. Call out a Clock Buddy time so that they can begin sharing their response to the questions (i.e., meet with your 3:00 Buddy, etc.). Repeat the process with a new Clock Buddy (no more than 2 minutes for each Clock Buddy round). 
  5. Once done, return to the community circle and invite a few students to share their responses and something they learned from their partners. 
  6. Have students turn in their Clock Buddies sheets before the end of the period and redistribute them the following day so that they can use them for additional partner activities.
  7. Remind the students of LIA’s mission statement, “To empower Latino youth through culture, service, leadership, and excellent education with the sole purpose of graduating from college.” Make sure that it is posted in a visible location.

  

 Debrief (3 min): (Reflection Model, Rolfe, 2001)

  • What? What were your thoughts and feelings as you signed up for your Clock Buddies? (Self-Awareness)
  1. So What? Why do you think it’s important to get to know how other students will be preparing for the ACT or SAT Practice Test? (Social Awareness)
  2. Now What? What will you do with what you learned about strategies to prepare for the ACT or SAT Practice Test? (Relationship Skills and Self-Awareness)

 

Current Event Bell Starter

Relevancy/Linkage

  • Review the previous lesson.
  • Last time we took the English portion of the ACT or SAT test, today we will be practicing the math portion.
  • Choose a math joke from 3.03 Weblink Math Joke to share with the students.
  • Ask them the following questions.
  • How many of you enjoy math, why or why not?
  • Why do you think math is a required section in both the ACT and SAT test?

  • Go to 3.03 Weblink Practice Test or another free ACT/SAT practice test website. Note: When signing in with mac & using the safari browser, you must enable pop-ups by going to settings in Safari preferences.  Click on Security and uncheck “Block pop-up windows”.  Then click on privacy.  Locate “Block cookies and other website data” and select “never” from the list.
  • If needed, remind the students how to log in. Encourage the students to write down their login information.
  • Go to College Prep and choose either the ACT or SAT test
  • Choose math for ACT or SAT

Reminder: If you create an account as well and give the students your ID and Last name they can click on  “Add Monitor”, which will allow you to view their test progress and results.

Independent Practice

  • Allow students as much time as possible to take the math portion of their chosen test.

  • Create an online SAT or ACT practice test of the most common wrong answers noted on the MATH practice test.  Google forms or online polling applications, such as Mentimeter, Kahoot!, Socrative, or Quizziz, provide insight into levels of understanding and inform instruction to better meet the needs of English Learners. Students can effectively review missed questions by identifying the type of question, determining the strategy, and internalizing the concepts.  
  • Ask the students to take a screenshot to print or email results, if they did not add the teacher as a monitor.
  • Assist students in finding explanations to questions they missed or do not understand.

  • Allow students time to review their correct and incorrect answers.
  • Pair students in groups of 2 or 3, and have the students learn and teach a concept or problem that they answered incorrectly.
  • Use other resources to help students prepare for the ACT/SAT test. See 3.01 ACT/SAT Resource Overview Page.

JOURNAL ENTRY SUGGESTIONS

  • What can I do to improve my math ACT/SAT test scores?
  • Students can create video journals to document their personal growth, self-reflect, and share their thoughts and experiences. All major Learning Management Systems (LMS) support student recordings within the interface such as Screencastify Submit with Google Classroom or Canvas.

OBJECTIVES:

Students will: 

  • take the reading portion of the ACT or SAT practice test
  • understand that effort and practice help build confidence and that feeling confident helps you do your best and makes you proud (Self-Awareness)
  • Understand the impact of developing self-discipline and self-motivation (Self-Management) 
  • demonstrate appropriate social behaviors to improve success, i.e., ask permission, ask for help, offer help to others, and contribute to the community. (Self-Management)
  • recognize the importance of effort in goal attainment (Self-Management)

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner column_margin="default" column_direction="default" column_direction_tablet="default" column_direction_phone="default" text_align="left" row_position="default" row_position_tablet="inherit" row_position_phone="inherit" overflow="visible" pointer_events="all"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_tablet="inherit" column_padding_phone="inherit" column_padding_position="all" column_element_direction_desktop="default" column_element_spacing="default" desktop_text_alignment="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_backdrop_filter="none" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" overflow="visible" gradient_direction="left_to_right" overlay_strength="0.3" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" animation_type="default" bg_image_animation="none" border_type="simple" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text]WELCOMING ACTIVITY

Purpose: To facilitate and encourage student interaction through the use of the Clock Buddies (Part 3) tool so that students will have specific partners to discuss their strategies to better prepare for the ACT or SAT Reading Practice Test. This is a quick and easy way to create pairs for the rest of the partnered activities related to the other practice tests. 

Skills for Learning and Life Focus: Interacting with Clock Buddies will further enhance students’ competencies of Self-Awareness, Relationship Skills, and Self-Management.

Overview:

  1. Welcome students - lead a Community Circle/ Class Meeting activity, see (Optional)
    • Skills for Learning and Life Signature Practices Playbook
    • Introduction to Welcoming Rituals
    • Greetings
  1. Dedicate time in your Community Circles/ Class Meetings to establish norms of collaboration on:
    1. how to greet each other once they meet their new Clock Buddy, 
    2. have them practice pronouncing each other's first and last names properly, 
    3. how they will ensure that each partner has equal time, and 
    4. how to thank each other once they have completed their activity instead of just walking away once the time is up. 
  2. Make copies of the Clock Buddy handout and distribute it to each student and ask them to write their own name at the top of their paper. Follow the procedures for HS Lesson 3.02.
  3. On a 5x8 card or a sheet of paper, ask students to write down a response to a prompt you give related to their own strategies in taking the Reading portion of the ACT or SAT Practice Test. For example:
    1. Name three steps you can take to better prepare for the Reading Practice Test.
    2. Which areas in Reading do you feel more confident that you will do well on the test? Which areas do you feel the least prepared for (i.e., comprehension, vocabulary, fluency, etc.)?
    3. What steps will you take to improve on your areas of greatest need?
  4. Call out a Clock Buddy time so that they can begin sharing their response to the questions (i.e., meet with your 3:00 Buddy, etc.). Repeat the process with a new Clock Buddy (no more than 2 minutes for each Clock Buddy round). 
  5. Once done, return to the community circle and invite a few students to share their responses and something they learned from their partners. 
  6. Have students turn in their Clock Buddies sheets before the end of the period and redistribute them the following day so that they can use them for additional partner activities.
  7. Remind the students of LIA’s mission statement, “To empower Latino youth through culture, service, leadership, and excellent education with the sole purpose of graduating from college.” Make sure that it is posted in a visible location.

  

 Debrief (3 min): (Reflection Model, Rolfe, 2001)

  • What? What were your thoughts and feelings as you signed up for your Clock Buddies? (Self-Awareness)
  1. So What? Why do you think it’s important to get to know how other students will be preparing for the ACT or SAT Practice Test? (Social Awareness)
  2. Now What? What will you do with what you learned about strategies to prepare for the ACT or SAT Practice Test? (Relationship Skills and Self-Awareness)

 

Current Event Bell Starter

Relevancy/Linkage

  • Review the previous lesson.
  • Last time we took the math portion of the ACT or SAT test, today we will be practicing the reading portion.
  • Show the students one or more of the following test-taking memes: 3.04 Meme 1, 3.04 Meme 2, 3.04 Meme 3, 3.04 Meme 4. Ask students the following questions:
    • Has this ever happened to you?
    • What strategies do you use to better manage your time to prepare for a test?
    • What are the advantages of taking practice tests?

  • Go to 3.04 Weblink Practice Test or another free ACT/SAT practice test website. Note: When signing in with mac & using the Safari browser, you must enable pop-ups by going to settings in Safari preferences.  Click on Security and uncheck “Block pop-up windows”.  Then click on privacy.  Locate “Block cookies and other website data” and select “never” from the list.
  • Show the students how to create an account and log in. Encourage the students to write down their login information.
  • Go to College Prep and choose either the ACT or SAT test.
  • Choose Reading for ACT or Critical Reading for SAT.

Note: If you create an account as well and give the students your ID and Last name they can click on  “Add Monitor”, which will allow you to view their test progress and results.

Independent Practice

  • Allow students as much time as possible to take the English or Writing portion of their chosen test.

  • Create an online SAT or ACT practice test of the most common wrong answers noted on the READING practice test. Google forms or online polling applications, such as Mentimeter, Kahoot!, Socrative, or Quizziz, provide insight into levels of understanding and inform instruction to better meet the needs of English Learners. Students can effectively review missed questions by identifying the type of question, determining the strategy, and internalizing the concepts.  
  • Ask the students to take a screenshot to print or email results, if they did not add the teacher as a monitor.
  • Assist students in finding explanations to questions they missed or do not understand.

  • This is an alternative test prep website (can be used as a guest or by creating an account). Students may find this site more helpful and interactive.
  • 3.04 Weblink ACT Test Prep
  • Allow students to take other postsecondary entrance exams, such as the ASVAB or other technical school entrance exams.
  • Please consider this lesson as optional if there is minimal time to administer and review the practice test. 

Extension

  • Allow students time to review their correct and incorrect answers.
  • Pair students in groups of 2 or 3, and have the students teach a concept or problem that they answered incorrectly.
  • Use other resources to help students prepare for the ACT/SAT test. See 3.01 ACT/SAT Resource Overview.

Journal Entry Suggestions 

  • What are some strategies to help me calm down before a test?
  • How can I be more prepared for taking tests?
  • Students can create video journals to document their personal growth, self-reflect, and share their thoughts and experiences. All major Learning Management Systems (LMS) support student recordings within the interface such as Screencastify Submit with Google Classroom or Canvas.

OBJECTIVES:

Students will: 

  • take the science or essay portion of the ACT or SAT practice test.
  • understand that effort and practice help build confidence and that feeling confident helps you do your best and makes you proud (Self-Awareness)
  • Understand the impact of developing self-discipline and self-motivation (Self-Management) 
  • demonstrate appropriate social behaviors to improve success, i.e., ask permission, ask for help, offer help to others, and contribute to the community. (Self-Management)
  • recognize the importance of effort in goal attainment (Self-Management)

  • WELCOMING ACTIVITY Purpose: To facilitate and encourage student interaction through the use of the Clock Buddies (Part 4) tool so that students will have specific partners to discuss their strategies to better prepare for the ACT or SAT Science or Essay Practice Test. This is a quick and easy way to create pairs for the rest of the partnered activities related to the other practice tests. Skills for Learning and Life Focus: Interacting with Clock Buddies will further enhance students’ competencies of Self-Awareness, Relationship Skills, and Self-Management.Overview:
    1. Welcome students - lead a Community Circle/ Class Meeting activity, see (Optional)
    • Skills for Learning and Life Signature Practices Playbook 
    • Introduction to Welcoming Rituals
    • Greetings
    1. Dedicate time in your Community Circles/ Class Meetings to establish norms of collaboration on:
      1. how to greet each other once they meet their new Clock Buddy, 
      2. have them practice pronouncing each other's first and last names properly, 
      3. how they will ensure that each partner has equal time, and 
      4. how to thank each other once they have completed their activity instead of just walking away once the time is up. 
    2. Make copies of the Clock Buddy handout and distribute it to each student and ask them to write their own name at the top of their paper. Follow the procedures for HS Lesson 3.02.
    3. On a 5x8 card or a sheet of paper, ask students to write down a response to a prompt you give related to their own strategies in taking the Science or Essay portion of the ACT or SAT Practice Test. For example:
      1. Name three steps you can take to better prepare for the Science or Essay Practice Test.
      2. Which areas in Science or Essay writing do you feel more confident that you will do well on the test? Which areas do you feel the least prepared for (i.e., vocabulary, concepts, writing, etc.)?
      3. What steps will you take to improve on your areas of greatest need?
    4. Call out a Clock Buddy time so that they can begin sharing their response to the questions (i.e., meet with your 3:00 Buddy, etc.). Repeat the process with a new Clock Buddy (no more than 2 minutes for each Clock Buddy round). 
    5. Once done, return to the community circle and invite a few students to share their responses and something they learned from their partners. 
    6. Have students turn in their Clock Buddies sheets before the end of the period and redistribute them the following day so that they can use them for additional partner activities.
    7. Remind the students of LIA’s mission statement, “To empower Latino youth through culture, service, leadership, and excellent education with the sole purpose of graduating from college.” Make sure that it is posted in a visible location.

      

     Debrief (3 min): (Reflection Model, Rolfe, 2001)

    • What? What were your thoughts and feelings as you signed up your Clock Buddies? (Self-Awareness)
    1. So What? Why do you think it’s important to get to know how other students will be preparing for the ACT or SAT Practice Test? (Social Awareness)
    2. Now What? What will you do with what you learned about strategies to prepare for the ACT or SAT Practice Test? (Relationship Skills and Self-Awareness)

     

    Current Event Bell Starter

    Relevancy/Linkage

    • Review the previous lesson:
    • Last time we took the reading portion of the ACT or SAT test, today we will be practicing the science portion.
    • Show the students one or more of the following memes: 3.05 Meme 1, 3.05 Meme 2, 3.05 Meme 3. Ask students the following questions:
      • Why do you think it’s important to prepare for the ACT/SAT?
      • What ACT/SAT study tips have you found useful?
      • Where can you go in the community or at school for ACT/SAT preparation help?

  • Go to 3.05 Weblink Practice Test or another free ACT/SAT practice test website. Note: When signing in with mac & using the safari browser, you must enable pop-ups by going to settings in Safari preferences.  Click on Security and uncheck “Block pop-up windows”.  Then click on privacy.  Locate “Block cookies and other website data” and select “never” from the list.
  • Show the students how to create an account and log in. Encourage the students to write down their login information.
  • Go to College Prep and choose either the ACT or SAT test.
  • Choose Science for ACT or Essay for SAT.
  • Note: If you create an account as well and give the students your ID and Last name they can click on  “Add Monitor”, which will allow you to view their test progress and results.

Independent Practice

  • Allow students as much time as possible to take the English or Writing portion of their chosen test.

  • Create an online SAT or ACT practice test of the most common wrong answers noted on the SCIENCE or ESSAY practice test.  Google forms or online polling applications, such as Mentimeter, Kahoot!, Socrative, or Quizziz, provide insight into levels of understanding and inform instruction to better meet the needs of English Learners. Students can effectively review missed questions by identifying the type of question, determining the strategy, and internalizing the concepts.  
  • Ask the students to take a screenshot to print or email results, if they did not add the teacher as a monitor.
  • Assist students in finding explanations to questions they missed or do not understand.
  • Inform the students that today is the last day of practice tests. Encourage them to take additional, full-length practice tests at home.

  • This is an alternative test prep website (can be used as a guest or by creating an account). Students may find this site more helpful and interactive.
  • 3.02 Weblink ACT Test Prep
  • Allow students to take other postsecondary entrance exams, such as the ASVAB or other technical school entrance exams.
  • This lesson is optional if there is minimal time to administer and review the practice test.

Extension

  • Allow students time to review their correct and incorrect answers.
  • Pair students in groups of 2 or 3, and have the students teach a concept or problem that they answered incorrectly.
  • Use other resources to help students prepare for the ACT/SAT test. See 3.01 ACT/SAT Resource Overview.

Journal Entry Suggestions

  • What skills do I excel at for test-taking? What areas can I improve in?
  • Explain your plan for preparing for and taking the ACT/SAT.
  • Students can create video journals to document their personal growth, self-reflect, and share their thoughts and experiences. All major Learning Management Systems (LMS) support student recordings within the interface such as Screencastify Submit with Google Classroom or Canvas.

OBJECTIVES:

Students will: 

  • learn about the branches of the armed forces, career options, and educational benefits.
  • identify and explore ways to develop skills and talents (Self-Awareness)
  •  understand the impact of developing self-discipline and self-motivation (Self-Management)
  • recognize various jobs and the responsibilities the jobs hold (Self-Management)
  • identify future careers that are aligned to personal interests, skills, and goals (Responsible Decision-Making)
  • identify and demonstrate skills for joining a group (Relationship Skills)

INTRODUCTION

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner column_margin="default" column_direction="default" column_direction_tablet="default" column_direction_phone="default" text_align="left" row_position="default" row_position_tablet="inherit" row_position_phone="inherit" overflow="visible" pointer_events="all"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_tablet="inherit" column_padding_phone="inherit" column_padding_position="all" column_element_direction_desktop="default" column_element_spacing="default" desktop_text_alignment="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_backdrop_filter="none" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" overflow="visible" gradient_direction="left_to_right" overlay_strength="0.3" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" animation_type="default" bg_image_animation="none" border_type="simple" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]WELCOMING ACTIVITY

Purpose: To encourage students to identify career options while serving their country. Students will think about serving in the armed forces and consider the advantages of this career option through the use of the Imagine (Part 1) activity.  

Skills for Learning and Life Focus: This Imagine activity will further enhance students’ competencies of Self-Awareness, Social Awareness, and Responsible Decision-Making.

Overview: 

  1. Welcome students - lead a Community Circle/ Class Meetings activity, see (Optional)
    • Skills for Learning and Life Signature Practices Playbook 
    • Introduction to Welcoming Rituals
    • Greetings
  1. While still in the Community Circle, have students close their eyes and envision serving in the armed forces and the advantages associated with serving in the military. Teachers might need to preface this activity with a lesson about what students know about the armed forces, what it means, and what the branches of the military are.
  2. As you read the four questions, take 30 seconds to have them reflect on their response for each one. Post the prompts in a visible location (whiteboard, Smartboard, or anchor chart) or have them printed out on a handout:
    1. What career options have you considered?
    2. What benefits or advantages would there be in serving in the armed forces to further your career goals?
    3. What branch of the military would you be most interested in?
    4. What requirements would you need to fulfill before enlisting in the military? 
  3. Ask students to write down a short response to each of the four prompts on a sheet of paper.
  4. Have them Turn and Talk to an elbow partner and share each response. 
  5. Now have them write a response to this 5th question: 

e. List any changes in your long term goals that you would have to make in order to serve in the armed forces. 

  1. Once they have completed the 5th question, use the "Mix and mingle" activity with music (use samples of culturally familiar music such as cumbias, salsa, merengue, bachata, Norteños, mariachi, reggaeton, etc) to have students find a different partner to compare their responses to the 5th prompt.
  2. Partners share their responses, listen actively to each other, ask follow-up questions, and debate any differences of opinion that they may have.
  3. Start the music again and repeat the sequence with another partner or two, as time permits.
  4. Remind the students of LIA’s mission statement, “To empower youth through culture, service, leadership, and excellent education with the sole purpose of graduating from college.” Make sure that it is posted in a visible location.

Debrief (3 min): (Reflection Model, Rolfe, 2001)

  1. What? What were your thoughts and feelings as you participated in this activity? (Self-Awareness)
  2. So What? Why do you think it’s important to explore and share your own ideas  with other students about serving in the armed forces and the benefits of this career option? (Social Awareness) 
  3. Now What? What will you do with what you learned about other students’ ideas about serving in the armed forces? (Self Management)

 

Current Event Bell Starter

Relevancy/Linkage

  • Review the previous lesson:
  • Last time we took our final ACT or SAT practice test. Hopefully, you feel more confident in taking the test and finding additional practice resources. Today we will begin to explore post-high school options. One post-school option is joining the armed forces. We will explore armed forces career options along with tuition assistance and educational benefits. Regardless of whether you are interested in joining the armed forces or not, we want you to be educated in the basics and have the information needed to make an informed decision either way.
  • Show the students 3.06 Video Armed Forces and ask them the following questions:
  • What are the five branches of the U.S. Military?
  • Which branch is considered the cream of the crop?
  • If you wanted to become a pilot, which branch(s) would be the best option for you?
  • Invite students to read the following articles on how the military can help pay for college and career training:   
    • Today's Military- Paying for College
    • Military One Source - How the Military Helps Pay for College and Job Training

Prior to this lesson, have your Professional Committee reach out to your local military recruitment office or other qualified speaker to secure a guest speaker for your class period. 

  • Distribute the optional 3.06 HO Armed Forces Information (English) or 3.06 HO Armed Forces Information (Spanish) to each student before the guest speaker begins. Encourage the students to use this handout as a note-taking guide, keeping in mind the speaker may or may not discuss all the topics.
  • Introduce and turn the remaining time over to the guest speaker.

Guest Speaker - Activity 2

  • Invite active military personnel or a military veteran to speak with students about their experiences in the military. Utilize Google Meet or Zoom to engage students in a live interactive session. The interview should ensure ethnic and linguistic diversity in connecting students with a guest speaker that they can personally identify with. Students can prepare questions prior to the session. Some sample questions are:
    • When did you know you wanted to join the military?
    • What does your typical day look like in the military?
    • Have you taken classes to advance your career in the military?
    • What is the biggest challenge to achieving success in the military?
    • What advice would you give to your younger self at the start of your career in the military?

ADAPTATIONS

  • Allow the students to use the 3.06 Weblink Military to complete the handout if a guest speaker is not able to attend.
  • Ask the recruiter about options for Non-U.S. citizens. There are restrictions, but you do not necessarily have to be a U.S. Citizen to join the armed forces. Also, view 3.06 Weblink Non-Citizens for more information.

Extension

  • Allow students additional time to browse 3.06 Weblink Military or a specific branch they are interested in.
  • Read the article: “Latinos are fastest growing population in US military, but higher ranks remain out of reach”
    • Discuss challenges faced by different groups in the military. Examples can include:
      • Representation within high-ranking officer positions 
      • Education and language barriers 
      • Challenges with fairness in the military
    • Discuss behaviors and actions that can help people be successful in the military and achieve higher ranks. 

Journal Entry Suggestions

  • What values do the armed forces and LIA have in common? How would these values help you in life?
  • What benefits and opportunities are available in the armed forces?
  • Students can create video journals to document their personal growth, self-reflect, and share their thoughts and experiences. All major Learning Management Systems (LMS) support student recordings within the interface such as Screencastify Submit with Google Classroom or Canvas.

OBJECTIVE:

Students will: 

  • take a more in-depth look at three postsecondary education options.
  • understand that effort and practice help build confidence and that feeling confident helps you do your best and makes you proud (Self-Awareness)
  • Understand the impact of developing self-discipline and self-motivation (Self-Management) 
  • demonstrate appropriate social behaviors to improve success, i.e., ask permission, ask for help, offer help to others, and contribute to the community. (Self-Management)
  • recognize the importance of effort in goal attainment (Self-Management)

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner column_margin="default" column_direction="default" column_direction_tablet="default" column_direction_phone="default" text_align="left" row_position="default" row_position_tablet="inherit" row_position_phone="inherit" overflow="visible" pointer_events="all"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_tablet="inherit" column_padding_phone="inherit" column_padding_position="all" column_element_direction_desktop="default" column_element_spacing="default" desktop_text_alignment="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_backdrop_filter="none" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" overflow="visible" gradient_direction="left_to_right" overlay_strength="0.3" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" animation_type="default" bg_image_animation="none" border_type="simple" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]WELCOMING ACTIVITY

Purpose: To encourage students to identify higher education while considering career options. Students think about exploring postsecondary education and consider career options by getting a college degree through the use of the Imagine (Part 2) activity. 

Skills for Learning and Life Focus: This Imagine activity will further enhance students’ competencies of Self-Awareness, Social Awareness, and Responsible Decision-Making.

Overview: 

  1. Welcome students - lead a Community Circle/ Class Meetings activity, see (Optional)
      • Skills for Learning and Life Signature Practices Playbook 
      • Introduction to Welcoming Rituals
      • Greetings
  1. While still in the Community Circle, have students close their eyes and envision career options they want to consider and the college degree(s) needed to pursue that career. 
  2. As you read the four prompts, take 30 seconds to have them reflect on each. Post the prompts in a visible location (whiteboard, Smartboard, or anchor chart) or have them printed out on a handout:
    1. What career options have you considered? 
    2. What benefits or advantages would there be in getting a college degree to further your career goals?
    3. Which field of study would you be most interested in?
    4. What requirements would you need to fulfill before reaching your career goals?
  3. Ask students to write down a short response to each of the four prompts on a sheet of paper.
  4. Have them Turn and Talk to an elbow partner and share each response. 
  5. Now have them write a response to this 5th prompt: 

e.  List any changes in your current studies and study habits that you would have to make in order to realize your long-term career goals. 

  1. Once completed use the "Mix and Mingle!" activity with music (use samples of culturally familiar music such as cumbias, salsa, merengue, bachata, Norteños, mariachi, reggaeton, etc) to have students find a different partner to compare their responses to the 5th prompt.
  2. Partners share their responses, listen actively to each other, ask follow-up questions and debate any differences of opinion that they may have.
  3. Start the music again and repeat the sequence with another partner or two, as time permits.
  4. Remind the students of LIA’s mission statement, “To empower Latino youth through culture, service, leadership, and excellent education with the sole purpose of graduating from college.” Make sure that it is posted in a visible location.

Debrief (3 min): (Reflection Model, Rolfe, 2001)

  1. What? What were your thoughts and feelings as you participated in this activity? (Self-Awareness)
  2. So What? Why do you think it’s important to explore and share your own ideas with other students about exploring postsecondary education and the advantages of considering career options? (Social Awareness) 
  3. Now What? What will you do with what you learned about other students’ ideas about career options and the college degree(s) needed to pursue that career? (Self Management)

Current Event Bell Starter

Relevancy/Linkage

  • Review the previous lesson:
  • Last time we explored options and benefits within the armed forces. Today we will take a more in-depth look at postsecondary schools of interest.
    • Show the students one or both of the following videos: 3.07 Video: Post Secondary Planning or 3.07 Video: Options After High School.
    • Ask them the following questions:
      • What are your attitudes toward the future?
      • What can you do now so things are more likely to fall into place when you are older?
      • What can you do now to increase your chances of getting accepted to college?
