[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner column_margin="default" column_direction="default" column_direction_tablet="default" column_direction_phone="default" text_align="left" row_position="default" row_position_tablet="inherit" row_position_phone="inherit" overflow="visible" pointer_events="all"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_tablet="inherit" column_padding_phone="inherit" column_padding_position="all" column_element_direction_desktop="default" column_element_spacing="default" desktop_text_alignment="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_backdrop_filter="none" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" overflow="visible" gradient_direction="left_to_right" overlay_strength="0.3" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" animation_type="default" bg_image_animation="none" border_type="simple" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text text_direction="default"]
Lesson steps
  • (I do) Explain to students that they will be interviewing each other to create a collection of class strengths and attributes. (slide #6)
  • (We do) Ask students to come up with interview questions and qualities or behaviors of a good interviewer. (slide #6)
ADAPTATION: have students write answers in their journals before sharing out to provide thinking time. ADAPTATION: provide a pre-generated list of questions to students. 
  • (You Do) Students conduct interviews. Be sure to adjust the highlighted text for your class (slide #7). ADAPTATION: have students interview in small groups and then compare notes afterward.  
Reflection: WHAT? | SO WHAT? | NOW WHAT? (slide #8) Initiate reflection using the questions below. Students can reflect quietly or in writing before sharing out in pairs, as a group, or as a class. 
  • What? What were your thoughts and feelings as you participated in this activity?
  • So what? Why do you think it’s important to get to know the people in your LIA class?
  • Now what? What will you do with what you learned about the interview process and your classmates?
Lesson closure
    • Students will present their interviewee to the class in a positive, kind way. Each presentation should highlight the student’s strengths and interests, their contributions to the class, and a picture. EXTENSION: integrate technology by allowing students to take pictures with a digital camera, smart phone, or tablet.
  • ADAPTATION: allow students to create a clip art or digital art instead of using a picture if they prefer not to have their picture taken. 
Virtual Class Adaptations:  
  • Conduct the lesson on an established LMS or use tools such as FlipGrid, Canvas, Miro, Google Classroom, or other interactive platform. 
  • Create a padlet and allow students to type their culture sentence into the padlet. 
  • Invite students to use the chat option to share their responses.

  1. How will practicing interviews help you in life?
  2. How did you feel interviewing and being interviewed?

DIFFERENTIATION: 
  • Use sentence stems to guide student conversations. 
  • Have students write their responses to each question in a journal or worksheet before sharing out loud. 
  • Provide a pre-generated list of questions for students to choose from. 
  • Provide a template for students to fill out so that everybody’s interview is the same. 
EXTENSION: 
  • Conduct research or read Carlos Santana’s history. https://www.britannica.com/biography/Carlos-Santana 
  • Vocabulary support. Students enhance vocabulary by using a search engine or thesaurus to find synonyms for their descriptive words. 
  • Create a physical or digital “book” to give to each student of the class as a memory/keepsake.

(self-awareness, self-management, social awareness, social management, social engagement).  LIA Themes: Cultural Enrichment, Team Building, Leadership, Professionalism, Responsive Conflict Resolution Setting the Stage Display the quote on the board and have students respond to one of the prompts as they get in their seats.  OPTIONAL: Play culturally relevant music as students enter the class. OPTIONAL: Lead students in a midline crossing activity. Use Educational Kinesiology document to find useful resources.  60-120 minute lesson OBJECTIVES: Students will
  • Develop and enhance their linguistic proficiency (2.1).
  • Develop social skills to interact across a wide variety of age groups and social contexts (2.2A, 2.2B, and 2.2C).
  • Students will use reflection and metacognition to develop critical thinking skills (2.3.)
  • Students will demonstrate an understanding of professional dress, appropriate behavior, and language across a variety of settings (3.1.A.)
  • Increase interpersonal skills through interactive games and situational practice (5.2.A.)
  • Identify and raise questions about what might be unexplained, missing, or left unsaid (WIDA ELD-SI.4-12.Narrate)
  • Report on explicit and inferred characteristics, patterns or behavior (WIDA ELD-SI.4-12.Inform)
  • Support or challenge an opinion, premise, or interpretation (WILDA ELD-SI.4-12.Argue).

Communication R.10 Slide Deck
Review objectives of the lesson with students (slide #5)
As students take their seats Students will respond to the prompt in their journal / daily worksheet. Prompt suggestions:
  • How has bilingualism benefited you?
  • Do you believe this quote? Why or why not. 
Provide 5-7 minutes for students to write their reflections. Display a timer on the board if able.  OPTIONAL: Ask students to share reflections. They can pair-share, group-share in tables, or volunteer responses to the class.  For virtual class: 
  • Allow students to use the chat, a discussion board, or unmute their microphones to share responses with the class.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner column_margin="default" column_direction="default" column_direction_tablet="default" column_direction_phone="default" text_align="left" row_position="default" row_position_tablet="inherit" row_position_phone="inherit" overflow="visible" pointer_events="all"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_tablet="inherit" column_padding_phone="inherit" column_padding_position="all" column_element_direction_desktop="default" column_element_spacing="default" desktop_text_alignment="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_backdrop_filter="none" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" overflow="visible" gradient_direction="left_to_right" overlay_strength="0.3" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" animation_type="default" bg_image_animation="none" border_type="simple" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text text_direction="default"]
Lesson steps
  • (I do, We Do) Group students into pairs or threes at most. Distribute Communication Activity. Explain to students that one of them will be a reader (Student A), giving instructions, and the other (Student B) will be a drawer, listening to instructions. Instruct Student B that they will not interrupt or ask questions, they will just listen and do. 
  • (You Do) Ask students if anybody succeeded in drawing a chicken. 
    • If not, ask students to reflect and share the disconnect between the instructions and the drawing. 
    • If so, ask students to reflect and share what worked well in achieving the desired goal. 
ADAPTATION: teacher reads instructions to all students and they follow along.  Reflection: WHAT? | SO WHAT? | NOW WHAT? (slide #7) Initiate reflection using the questions below. Students can reflect quietly or in writing before sharing out in pairs, as a group, or as a class. 
  • What? What were your thoughts and feelings as you participated in this activity?
  • So what? Why do you think it’s important that all sides can participate in communicating with each other?
  • Now what? What will you do with what you’ve learned about communication today?
  • (I Do) Communication Styles (slides #8-11) . Teacher or student reads slide to the class. ADAPTATION: teacher provides examples of each communication style. EXTENSION: students come up with examples of each communication style. 
  • (We Do)Distribute SLANT Strategy to students for general suggestions of good communication. (slide #12)
  • (You Do) Does Culture Play a Role in Communication Style? (Slide #13) Recall individualist and collectivist cultures. Ask students to make inferences about culture and preferred communication style using the provided sentence frames. EXTENSION: students use a variation of the prompts provided to share their inferences. 
    • Individualists/collectivists are more likely to exhibit ________ communication style when they are ___________ (under pressure, upset, feeling great, etc) because….
    •  As someone who primarily identifies with individualist/collectivist culture, the communication style I was taught is the most polite is __________________. This is because…
  • (We Do) Denotation and Connotation (slide #14). Explain that words and behaviors can be interpreted differently, and share the examples in the slide. Ask students to share examples. 
  • (You Do) Communication & Technology (slide #15-#16) Students brainstorm individually, pairs, or small groups. They may write their answers on a worksheet or journal before sharing out. Ask students to volunteer answers for the board. EXTENSION: What advantages or disadvantages does technology have on communication?
  • Kinesthetic ADAPTATION: Four Corners Activity for opinions on slide #16. 
Virtual Class Adaptations:  
  • Conduct the lesson on an established LMS or use tools such as FlipGrid, Canvas, Miro, Google Classroom, or other interactive platform. 
  • Invite students to use the chat option to share their responses.

Exit ticket: Students complete one of the following prompts
  1. Something I learned today is…
  2. Some examples of good communication are…
In Person Class Assessment Options:
  • Write responses on a sticky note and place in a designated space in the classroom. 
  • Write in a journal / daily worksheet. 
  • Share out loud/with their groups
Virtual Class Assessment Options:
  • Discussion assignment on LMS.
  • Virtual board such as jamboard, miro, Zoom Whiteboard, etc.
  • Create a video on Flipgrid or Canvas.

ADAPTATIONS

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner column_margin="default" column_direction="default" column_direction_tablet="default" column_direction_phone="default" bottom_padding="7px" text_align="left" row_position="default" row_position_tablet="inherit" row_position_phone="inherit" overflow="visible" pointer_events="all"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_tablet="inherit" column_padding_phone="inherit" column_padding_position="all" column_element_direction_desktop="default" column_element_spacing="default" desktop_text_alignment="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_backdrop_filter="none" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" overflow="visible" gradient_direction="left_to_right" overlay_strength="0.3" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" animation_type="default" bg_image_animation="none" border_type="simple" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text text_direction="default"]
DIFFERENTIATION: 
  • Use sentence stems to guide student conversations. 
  • Have students write their responses to each question in a journal or worksheet before sharing out loud. 
EXTENSION: 
  • Conduct research or read Sandra Cisneros. https://www.britannica.com/search?query=sandra+cisneros 
  • Vocabulary support. Students enhance vocabulary by using a search engine or thesaurus to find synonyms for their descriptive words. 
  • Conduct a Socratic Seminar or small group discussions on the following prompts. There are no right or wrong answers, and it is important to provide a safe space for students to answer honestly.  
    • What improvements can/should be made to online communications? 
    • How can I improve my in-person and online communication?
    • How did technology support education during the pandemic? 
    • What can I do if I misunderstand somebody?

(Self-Awareness, Self-Management, Self-Efficacy, Social Management) LIA Themes: Team Building, Leadership, Professionalism, Responsive Conflict Resolution Setting the Stage Display the quote on the board and have students respond to one of the prompts as they get in their seats.  OPTIONAL: Play culturally relevant music as students enter the class. OPTIONAL: Lead students in a midline crossing activity. Use Educational Kinesiology document to find useful resources.  45-60 minute lesson OBJECTIVES: Students will
  • Develop and enhance their linguistic proficiency (2.1).
  • Demonstrate leadership skills (2.2.B.)
  • Students will use reflection and metacognition to develop critical thinking skills (2.3.)
  • Identify personal positive attributes, marketable skills, and talents they can offer (3.1.B.)
  • Develop the needed skills to be successful in honors, AP, and college-level courses in the future (3.2.B).
  • Students will learn the characteristics of being a good leader (5.1)
  • Evaluate changes in thinking, identifying-trade offs (WIDA ELD-SI.4-12.Argue).
  • Evaluate the impact of word choices (WIDA ELD-LA.4-5.Inform.Interpretive).

Strengths & Weaknesses (Grows & Glows) R.11 Slide Deck
Review objectives of the lesson with students (slide #5)
As students take their seats Students will respond to the prompt in their journal / daily worksheet. Prompt suggestions:
  • What is one of your strengths?
  • What is one of your weaknesses?
Provide 5-7 minutes for students to write their reflections. Display a timer on the board if able.  OPTIONAL: Ask students to share reflections. They can pair-share, group-share in tables, or volunteer responses to the class.  For virtual class: 
  • Allow students to use the chat, a discussion board, or unmute their microphones to share responses with the class.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner column_margin="default" column_direction="default" column_direction_tablet="default" column_direction_phone="default" text_align="left" row_position="default" row_position_tablet="inherit" row_position_phone="inherit" overflow="visible" pointer_events="all"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_tablet="inherit" column_padding_phone="inherit" column_padding_position="all" column_element_direction_desktop="default" column_element_spacing="default" desktop_text_alignment="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_backdrop_filter="none" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" overflow="visible" gradient_direction="left_to_right" overlay_strength="0.3" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" animation_type="default" bg_image_animation="none" border_type="simple" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text text_direction="default"]
Lesson steps
  • (I do) (slide #6) Distribute Loteria Card to all students. Explain that the purpose is to fill in the entire card with student signatures. After there are three winners OR after a determined amount of time, students will return to their seats. ADAPTATION: change the wording in the squares to better match the strengths you see in your class. ADAPTATION: modify the rules of the game as works best for your class. 
  • (You Do) Distribute a new card to all students and have them circle or write their names in the squares that apply to them, and an X over the squares that do not. 
  • (slide #7) On the back of the sheet or a separate sheet of paper, have students make a T chart of strengths (glows) and weaknesses (grows) from the Loteria card. EXTENSION: Invite students to think of other strengths or weaknesses to add to their chart. 
  • (I do) Read slide #8 to students, providing the examples in the notes section. 
  • (We do) Explain that fixed mindsets can be positive or negative self talk (slide #9), have students help fill out the chart. 
  • (You do) in small groups, students will brainstorm ways to turn their T-chart grows into glows (slide #10). 
Reflection: WHAT? | SO WHAT? | NOW WHAT? (slide #11) Initiate reflection using the questions below. Students can reflect quietly or in writing before sharing out in pairs, as a group, or as a class. 
  • What? What were your thoughts and feelings as you participated in this activity?
  • So what? Why do you think it’s important to have a growth mindset as a leader?
  • Now what? What will you do with what you’ve learned about growth mindset, strengths, and weaknesses today?
Virtual Class Adaptations:  
  • Conduct the lesson on an established LMS or use tools such as FlipGrid, Canvas, Miro, Google Classroom, or other interactive platform. 
  • Invite students to use the chat option to share their responses.

Exit ticket: Students complete one of the following prompts
  1. As a leader, why is it important to know your strengths and weaknesses?
  2. What are the benefits of having a growth mindset?
In Person Class Assessment Options:
  • Write responses on a sticky note and place in a designated space in the classroom. 
  • Write in a journal / daily worksheet. 
  • Share out loud/with their groups
Virtual Class Assessment Options:
  • Discussion assignment on LMS.
  • Virtual board such as jamboard, miro, Zoom Whiteboard, etc.
  • Create a video on Flipgrid or Canvas.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner column_margin="default" column_direction="default" column_direction_tablet="default" column_direction_phone="default" bottom_padding="7px" text_align="left" row_position="default" row_position_tablet="inherit" row_position_phone="inherit" overflow="visible" pointer_events="all"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_tablet="inherit" column_padding_phone="inherit" column_padding_position="all" column_element_direction_desktop="default" column_element_spacing="default" desktop_text_alignment="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_backdrop_filter="none" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" overflow="visible" gradient_direction="left_to_right" overlay_strength="0.3" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" animation_type="default" bg_image_animation="none" border_type="simple" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text text_direction="default"]
DIFFERENTIATION: 
  • Use sentence stems to guide student conversations. 
  • Have students write their responses to each question in a journal or worksheet before sharing out loud. 
EXTENSION: 
  • Conduct research or read Antonio Tijerino. https://hispanicheritage.org/staff-member/jose-antonio-tijerino/ 
  • Vocabulary support. Students enhance vocabulary by using a search engine or thesaurus to find synonyms for their descriptive words. 
  • Conduct a Socratic Seminar or small group discussions on the following prompts. There are no right or wrong answers, and it is important to provide a safe space for students to answer honestly.  
    • What can I do to strengthen my growth mindset?
    • What can I do when dealing with somebody with a fixed mindset?

(self-awareness, self-management, self-efficacy). 

LIA Themes: Cultural Enrichment, Team Building, Leadership, Professionalism, Responsive Conflict Resolution

Setting the Stage

Display the quote on the board and have students respond to one of the prompts as they get in their seats. 

OPTIONAL: Play culturally relevant music as students enter the class.

OPTIONAL: Lead students in a midline crossing activity. Use Educational Kinesiology document to find useful resources. 

60-120 minute lesson

OBJECTIVES:

Students will

  • Demonstrate leadership skills (2.2.B).
  • Practice and use action plans to define problems, brainstorm solutions, then form and implement plans to address them (2.3.A.)
  • Research, plan, and execute potential life/professional short/long term goals (3.1.C)
  • Be exposed to opportunities and needs to plan for their future (3.2.)
  • Clarify and elaborate ideas based on feedback (WIDA ELD-SI.4-12.Argue)

SMARTE goals

R.12 Slide Deck
Review objectives of the lesson with students (slide #5)

As students take their seats

Students will respond to the prompt in their journal / daily worksheet. Prompt suggestions:

  • How does education help you stand out?
  • Do you believe this quote? Why or why not. 

Provide 5-7 minutes for students to write their reflections. Display a timer on the board if able. 

OPTIONAL: Ask students to share reflections. They can pair-share, group-share in tables, or volunteer responses to the class. 

For virtual class: 

  • Allow students to use the chat, a discussion board, or unmute their microphones to share responses with the class.

Lesson steps

  • (I do) Explain to students what a SMARTE goal is (slide #6)
  • (We Do) (slide #7) Distribute LIA Student Standards and invite a student to read the mission statement out loud. Ask students to reflect on the following questions: 
    • Why do you think LIA is offered at your school?
    • Why did you decide to take LIA?
    • How has LIA helped you achieve the LIA mission?

Tell students they will be using the LIA Standards to write one personal and one academic goal for themselves to achieve by the end of the year.
ADAPTATION: the goals could be for the end of the quarter/semester instead of the year.  

  • (We Do) (slide #8) Explain to students that LIA class materials were created to help them achieve the LIA mission and that each of them have individual talents and dreams. 
  • (We Do) Display SMARTE GOAL template and with student input, set one SMARTE goal for the class. Work through each of the steps. This will serve as a scaffold for the next activity. 
  • (You Do) (slide #9) Distribute SMARTE GOAL template for students to fill out.
    OPTIONAL: have students recall some strengths or weaknesses from the previous lesson to help them set goals. If available, have students pull up their work from the previous lesson to jog their memory.,
    EXTENSION: ask students to share their goals with the class. 

Reflection: WHAT? | SO WHAT? | NOW WHAT? (slide #10)

Initiate reflection using the questions below. Students can reflect quietly or in writing before sharing out in pairs, as a group, or as a class. 

  • What? What were your thoughts and feelings as you participated in this activity?
  • So what? Why do you think it’s important to know about SMARTE goals?
  • Now what? What will you do with what you’ve learned about goal-setting?

Virtual Class Adaptations:  

  • Conduct the lesson on an established LMS or use tools such as FlipGrid, Canvas, Miro, Google Classroom, or other interactive platform. 
  • Invite students to use the chat option to share their responses.

Exit ticket: Students complete one of the following prompts

  1. My academic SMARTE goal is…
  2. My personal SMARTE goal is…

In Person Class Assessment Options:

  • Write responses on a sticky note and place in a designated space in the classroom. 
  • Write in a journal / daily worksheet. 
  • Share out loud/with their groups

Virtual Class Assessment Options:

  • Discussion assignment on LMS.
  • Virtual board such as jamboard, miro, Zoom Whiteboard, etc.
  • Create a video on Flipgrid or Canvas.

DIFFERENTIATION: 

  • Use sentence stems to guide student conversations. 
  • Have students write their responses to each question in a journal or worksheet before sharing out loud. 

EXTENSION: 

  • Conduct research or read about Ellen Ochoa.   
  • Vocabulary support. Students enhance vocabulary by using a search engine or thesaurus to find synonyms for their descriptive words. 
  • Conduct a Socratic Seminar or small group discussions on the following prompts. There are no right or wrong answers, and it is important to provide a safe space for students to answer honestly.  
    • How are SMARTE goals useful?
    • What is the difference between setting a goal and setting a SMARTE goal?
    • What can I do if I don’t meet my goals as expected?

OPTIONAL: Lead students in a midline crossing activity. Use Educational Kinesiology document to find useful resources.    45-90 minute lesson   OBJECTIVES: Students will
  • Students will use cultural knowledge to connect with and participate in family and school communities (1.1.).
  • Demonstrate leadership skills (2.2.B.).
  • Identify personal attributes, marketable skills, and talents they can offer to both employers and community (3.1.B.).
  • Develop the needed skills to be successful in honors, AP, and college-level courses in the future (3.2.B.).
  • Share ideas about one’s own and others’ lived experiences and previous learning (WIDA ELD-SI.4-12.Narrate).
  • Evaluate changes in thinking, identifying trade-offs (WIDA ELD-SI.4-12.Argue).
  • Describe components, order, causes and effects, or cycles using relevant examples and details (WIDA ELD-SS.4-5.Explain.Expressive)
  • Establish perspective (WIDA ELD-SS.4-5.Argue.Expressive)

Review objectives of the lesson with students (slide #5)
As students take their seats Students will respond to the prompt in their journal / daily worksheet. Prompt suggestions:
  • Do you agree or disagree? Explain your answer.
  • What is something you have done or want to do to make the world a better place?
Provide 5-7 minutes for students to write their reflections. Display a timer on the board if able.  OPTIONAL: Ask students to share reflections. They can pair-share, group-share in tables, or volunteer responses to the class.  For virtual class: 
  • Allow students to use the chat, a discussion board, or unmute their microphones to share responses with the class.

INSTRUCTION

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner column_margin="default" column_direction="default" column_direction_tablet="default" column_direction_phone="default" text_align="left" row_position="default" row_position_tablet="inherit" row_position_phone="inherit" overflow="visible" pointer_events="all"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_tablet="inherit" column_padding_phone="inherit" column_padding_position="all" column_element_direction_desktop="default" column_element_spacing="default" desktop_text_alignment="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_backdrop_filter="none" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" overflow="visible" gradient_direction="left_to_right" overlay_strength="0.3" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" animation_type="default" bg_image_animation="none" border_type="simple" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]Lesson steps
  • (I do) Read the fable to students on slide #6. ADAPTATION: prepare students by asking them if they know what a fable is. ADAPTATION: print out the story so students can follow along. 
 
  • (We Do) Students define “responsibility” with their table partners/groups. (slide #7). After they have had time to discuss, click to share the definition that is on the slide. ADAPTATION: students can write the definitions in their journals.  
  • (I Do) Read slide #8 to students. 
  • (You do) Students will work in pairs or small groups to make a list of the responsibilities they have at home and at school. When time has elapsed, ask some students to share their answers with the class. Write them on the board (or have students come up and write on the board). ADAPTATION: print out slide #9 so students can write on it. 
  • (We Do) Now that you have a list of home and school responsibilities, ask students to brainstorm who is affected by the responsibility (stakeholder), and what could happen if it does not get done (consequence). An example for each is provided. 
  Reflection: WHAT? | SO WHAT? | NOW WHAT? (slide #11) Initiate reflection using the questions below. Students can reflect quietly or in writing before sharing out in pairs, as a group, or as a class. 
  • What? What were your thoughts and feelings as you participated in this activity?
  • So what? Why do you think it’s important to fulfill your responsibilities?
  • Now what? What will you do with what you learned about responsibility today?
  Lesson closure 
  • Explain the circles of responsibility (slide #12) and distribute Circles of Responsibility Handout for them to fill out. 
EXTENSION: students present their responsibilities to the class.   Virtual Class Adaptations:  
  • Conduct the lesson on an established LMS or use tools such as FlipGrid, Canvas, Miro, Google Classroom, or other interactive platform. 
  • Create a padlet and allow students to type their reflections into the padlet. 
  • Invite students to use the chat option to share their responses.

ADAPTATIONS

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner column_margin="default" column_direction="default" column_direction_tablet="default" column_direction_phone="default" bottom_padding="7px" text_align="left" row_position="default" row_position_tablet="inherit" row_position_phone="inherit" overflow="visible" pointer_events="all"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_tablet="inherit" column_padding_phone="inherit" column_padding_position="all" column_element_direction_desktop="default" column_element_spacing="default" desktop_text_alignment="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_backdrop_filter="none" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" overflow="visible" gradient_direction="left_to_right" overlay_strength="0.3" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" animation_type="default" bg_image_animation="none" border_type="simple" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]DIFFERENTIATION: 
  • Use sentence stems to guide student conversations. 
  • Have students write their responses to each question in a journal or worksheet before sharing out loud. 
  EXTENSION: 
  • Conduct research or read Dolores Huerta’s history. https://www.britannica.com/biography/Dolores-Huerta
  • Vocabulary support. Students enhance vocabulary by using a search engine or thesaurus to find synonyms for their descriptive words. 
  • Conduct a Socratic Seminar or small group discussions on the following prompts. There are no right or wrong answers, and it is important to provide a safe space for students to answer honestly.  
    • Have you ever forgotten or ignored a responsibility? What was the outcome?
    • What can you do if you accidentally forget to follow through on a responsibility?
    • What is the difference in your responsibilities now and your responsibilities 1/2/3 years ago? 
    • What are some responsibilities you are looking forward to as you get older? Why?
  • Allow students to write their own fable.
  • Students will research Aesop. 
  • Students can write a different ending to the fable. For example, one where the grasshopper demonstrates responsibility, or one where the ant chooses to go have fun instead of being responsible.
  • Students create a play or skit to demonstrate their responsibilities, what happens if they do not fulfill them, and what happens if they do.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner column_margin="default" column_direction="default" column_direction_tablet="default" column_direction_phone="default" text_align="left" row_position="default" row_position_tablet="inherit" row_position_phone="inherit" overflow="visible" pointer_events="all"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_tablet="inherit" column_padding_phone="inherit" column_padding_position="all" column_element_direction_desktop="default" column_element_spacing="default" desktop_text_alignment="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_backdrop_filter="none" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" overflow="visible" gradient_direction="left_to_right" overlay_strength="0.3" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" animation_type="default" bg_image_animation="none" border_type="simple" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]Purpose: Students will define integrity and understand the value of acting with integrity.   (self-awareness, self-management, social awareness, relationship skills, responsible decision-making).  LIA Themes: Leadership, Team Building, Professionalism, Responsive Conflict Resolution   Setting the Stage Display the quote on the board and have students respond to one of the prompts as they get in their seats.    OPTIONAL: Play culturally relevant music as students enter the class. OPTIONAL: Lead students in a midline crossing activity. Use Educational Kinesiology document to find useful resources.    45-90 minute lesson   OBJECTIVES: Students will
  • Demonstrate leadership skills (2.2.B.).
  • Develop the needed skills to be successful in honors, AP, and college-level courses in the future (3.2.B.). 
  • Increase interpersonal skills through interactive games and situational practice (5.2.A.)
  • Identify and raise questions about what might be unexplained, missing, or left unsaid (WIDA ELD-SI.4-12.Narrate).
  • Generate questions about different perspectives (WIDA ELD-SI.4-12.Inform).
  • Develop story with complication and resolution, time and event sequences (WIDA ELD-LA.4-5.Narrate.Expressive). 
  • Analyze points of view about the same event or topic (WIDA ELD-LA.4-5.Argue.Interpretive). 
  • Generalize probable causes and effects of developments or events (WIDA ELD-SS.4-5.Explain.Expressive).

Integrity

21st Century Skills Skills for Learning and Life
Critical Thinking, Creativity, Collaboration, Communication, Flexibility, Leadership, Initiative, Productivity, Social Skills Self-Awareness, Self-Management, Social Awareness, Responsible Decision-Making, Relationship Skills

Integrity R.03 Slide Deck
Review objectives of the lesson with students (slide #5)
As students take their seats Students will respond to the prompt in their journal / daily worksheet. Prompt suggestions:
  • What do you think Sylvia was talking about?
  • What are your thoughts when you read this quote?
Provide 5-7 minutes for students to write their reflections. Display a timer on the board if able.  OPTIONAL: Ask students to share reflections. They can pair-share, group-share in tables, or volunteer responses to the class.  For virtual class: 
  • Allow students to use the chat, a discussion board, or unmute their microphones to share responses with the class.

LESSON

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner column_margin="default" column_direction="default" column_direction_tablet="default" column_direction_phone="default" text_align="left" row_position="default" row_position_tablet="inherit" row_position_phone="inherit" overflow="visible" pointer_events="all"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_tablet="inherit" column_padding_phone="inherit" column_padding_position="all" column_element_direction_desktop="default" column_element_spacing="default" desktop_text_alignment="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_backdrop_filter="none" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" overflow="visible" gradient_direction="left_to_right" overlay_strength="0.3" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" animation_type="default" bg_image_animation="none" border_type="simple" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]
Lesson steps 
  • (We do) Ask students if they know what integrity means. Split them into pairs or small groups to come up with a definition and example. Provide 3-5 minutes for this activity, or more if you would like them to come up with multiple examples. ADAPTATION: have students write answers in their journals before sharing out to provide thinking time. ADAPTATION: divide the students in half, and have half of them define integrity while the other half thinks of examples. ADAPTATION: use definition from the R.03 vocabulary slide deck and have students come up with examples. 
  • (We Do) Now that you have a definition and some examples, tell students that you will have some scenarios for them (slides #7-#9). In scenario 1 and 2, students will have two options to choose from. They should choose their option and discuss their selection. In scenario 3, students will come up with a response/next action. See slide notes for ADAPTATIONs
Reflection: WHAT? | SO WHAT? | NOW WHAT? (slide #10) Initiate reflection using the questions below. Students can reflect quietly or in writing before sharing out in pairs, as a group, or as a class. 
  • What? What were your thoughts and feelings as you participated in this activity?
  • So what? Why do you think it’s important to act with integrity?
  • Now what? What will you do with what you learned about integrity today?
Lesson closure 
  • (You Do) Explain to students that they will be placed in three groups and create skits based on the scenarios they are given. 
  • Distribute Integrity Scenario Handout to students once they are in groups. The document contains 3 scenarios; each group will receive one scenario. Students will create two skits for each scenario - one skit that demonstrates integrity, and one that does not demonstrate integrity. Each student will participate in the skit in some fashion - the needed roles are written on their handout. 
  • Set a timer so that students know how much time they have to prepare their skits. 
  • After each skit, the students will vote on which scenario demonstrated integrity. 
Virtual Class Adaptations:  
  • Conduct the lesson on an established LMS or use tools such as FlipGrid, Canvas, Miro, Google Classroom, or other interactive platform. 
  • Create a padlet and allow students to type their reflections into the padlet. 
  • Invite students to use the chat option to share their responses.

Exit ticket: Students complete one of the following prompts
  1. How does integrity align with LIA values?
  2. How can you demonstrate integrity? Give 3 examples. 
In Person Class Assessment Options:
  • Write responses on a sticky note and place in a designated space in the classroom. 
  • Write in a journal / daily worksheet. 
  • Share out loud/with their groups
Virtual Class Assessment Options:
  • Discussion assignment on LMS.
  • Virtual board such as jamboard, miro, Zoom Whiteboard, etc.
  • Create a video on Flipgrid or Canvas.

ADAPTATIONS

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner column_margin="default" column_direction="default" column_direction_tablet="default" column_direction_phone="default" bottom_padding="7px" text_align="left" row_position="default" row_position_tablet="inherit" row_position_phone="inherit" overflow="visible" pointer_events="all"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_tablet="inherit" column_padding_phone="inherit" column_padding_position="all" column_element_direction_desktop="default" column_element_spacing="default" desktop_text_alignment="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_backdrop_filter="none" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" overflow="visible" gradient_direction="left_to_right" overlay_strength="0.3" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" animation_type="default" bg_image_animation="none" border_type="simple" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]
DIFFERENTIATION: 
  • Use sentence stems to guide student conversations. 
  • Have students write their responses to each question in a journal or worksheet before sharing out loud. 
EXTENSION: 
  • Conduct research or read Sylvia Mendez’s history.  https://www.britannica.com/search?query=sylvia+mendez+ 
  • Vocabulary support. Students enhance vocabulary by using a search engine or thesaurus to find synonyms for their descriptive words. 
  • Conduct a Socratic Seminar or small group discussions on the following prompts. There are no right or wrong answers, and it is important to provide a safe space for students to answer honestly.  
    • What does integrity mean to you? 
    • Describe a situation where people might not act with integrity. 
    • Is it harder to act with integrity, or to act without integrity? Explain. 
    • Have you ever lacked integrity? How did it make you feel? 
    • Has an adult you know ever lacked integrity? How did it make you feel?

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner column_margin="default" column_direction="default" column_direction_tablet="default" column_direction_phone="default" text_align="left" row_position="default" row_position_tablet="inherit" row_position_phone="inherit" overflow="visible" pointer_events="all"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_tablet="inherit" column_padding_phone="inherit" column_padding_position="all" column_element_direction_desktop="default" column_element_spacing="default" desktop_text_alignment="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_backdrop_filter="none" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" overflow="visible" gradient_direction="left_to_right" overlay_strength="0.3" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" animation_type="default" bg_image_animation="none" border_type="simple" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]Purpose: Students will learn about functions in their brain which prevent and support decision-making, and practice taking accountability.  LIA Themes: Conflict Resolution; Leadership   Setting the Stage Display the quote on the board and have students respond to one of the prompts as they get in their seats.    OPTIONAL: Play culturally relevant music as students enter the class. OPTIONAL: Lead students in a midline crossing activity. Use Educational Kinesiology document to find useful resources.    45-90 minute lesson   OBJECTIVES: Students will
  • Develop and enhance their linguistic proficiency (2.1).
  • Demonstrate leadership skills (2.2.B.)
  • Demonstrate conflict resolution skills in relation to interpersonal relationships (2.2.C.)
  • Develop the needed skills to be successful in honors, AP, and college-level courses in the future (3.2.B.).
  • Learn the responsibilities of being a leader (5.2.).
  • Share ideas about one’s own and others’ lived experiences and previous learning (WIDA ELD-SI.4-12.Narrate).
  • Describe the parts and wholes of a system (WIDA ELD-SI.4-12.Inform).
  • Evaluate changes in thinking, identifying trade-offs (WIDA ELD-SI.4-12.Argue).
  • Interpret language arts arguments by analyzing points of view about the same event or topic (WIDA ELD-LA.4-5.Argue.Interpretive).
  • Obtaining and combining evidence and information to help explain how or why a phenomenon occurs (WIDA ELD-SC.4-5.Explain.Interpretive). 
  • Develop reasoning to show relationships between evidence and claims (WIDA ELD-SC.4-5.Explain.Expressive)
  • Construct social studies arguments that establish perspective (WIDA ELD-SS.4-5.Argue.Interpretive). 
  Vocabulary
Self-discipline Accountability Blame
  Competencies and Skills
21st Century Skills Skills for Learning and Life
Critical Thinking, Communication, Flexibility, Leadership, Initiative, Social Skills Self-Awareness, Self-Management, Social Awareness, Responsible Decision-Making, Relationship Skills

Accountability R.02 Slide Deck
Review objectives of the lesson with students (slide #5)
As students take their seats Students will respond to the prompt in their journal / daily worksheet. Prompt suggestions:
  • Do you agree with the quote? Why or why not? 
  • What does it mean to make the most of your day? 
Provide 5-7 minutes for students to write their reflections. Display a timer on the board if able.  OPTIONAL: Ask students to share reflections. They can pair-share, group-share in tables, or volunteer responses to the class.  For virtual class: 
  • Allow students to use the chat, a discussion board, or unmute their microphones to share responses with the class.

Lesson steps
  • The Human Brain’s Learning Center. (I do) Read slides #6-#10 to/with students.
    • At slide 10, shake up the glitter water bottle. Explain to students how an agitated or alert amygdala is similar to a shaken up water bottle with glitter inside. 
Reflection: WHAT? | SO WHAT? | NOW WHAT? (slide #11) Initiate reflection using the questions below. Students can reflect quietly or in writing before sharing out in pairs, as a group, or as a class. 
  • What? What were your thoughts and feelings as you participated in this activity?
  • So what? Why do you think it’s important to know the parts of the brain responsible for impulses and reasoning? (Social Awareness)
  • Now what? What will you do with what you learned about calm and agitated brains? (Responsible Decision Making)
Lesson steps
  • Self Discipline. (We do) Read slide #12 to students.
EXTENSION: have students come up with additional examples for taking accountability or passing blame. 
  • (You do) Practice! Read through the scenarios on slides #13-15. Ask students to come up with responses to the prompts using blame and taking accountability. ADAPTATION: students can write answers in their journal, pair-share, turn-and-talk, work in small groups before sharing out. 
Virtual Class Adaptations:  
  • Conduct the lesson on an established LMS or use tools such as FlipGrid, Canvas, Miro, Google Classroom, or other interactive platform. 
  • Create a padlet and allow students to type their reflections into the padlet. 
  • Invite students to use the chat option to share their responses.

Exit ticket: Students complete one of the following prompts
  1. What is something you can say to take accountability rather than passing the blame?
  2. How does taking accountability align with LIA values?

  • Write responses on a sticky note and place in a designated space in the classroom. 
  • Write in a journal / daily worksheet. 
  • Share out loud/with their groups

  • Discussion assignment on LMS.
  • Virtual board such as jamboard, miro, Zoom Whiteboard, etc.
  • Create a video on Flipgrid or Canvas.

DIFFERENTIATION: 
  • Use sentence stems to guide student conversations. 
  • Have students write their responses to each question in a journal or worksheet before sharing out loud. 
  • Provide a pre-generated list of questions for students to choose from. 
  • Provide a template for students to fill out so that everybody’s interview is the same. 
EXTENSION: 
  • Conduct research or read Gabriela Mistral’s history. https://www.britannica.com/biography/Gabriela-Mistral 
  • Vocabulary support. Students enhance vocabulary by using a search engine or thesaurus to find synonyms for their descriptive words.

(self-awareness, self-management, social awareness, relationship skills, responsible decision-making).  LIA Themes: Academic Excellence, Team Building, Leadership, Professionalism, Service Learning   Setting the Stage Display the quote on the board and have students respond to one of the prompts as they get in their seats.    OPTIONAL: Play culturally relevant music as students enter the class. OPTIONAL: Lead students in a midline crossing activity. Use Educational Kinesiology document to find useful resources.    45-90 minute lesson   OBJECTIVES: Students will
  • Use cultural knowledge to connect with and participate in family and school communities (1.1.).
  • Demonstrate leadership skills (2.2.B.). 
  • Identify personal positive attributes, marketable skills, and talents that they can offer to employers and community (3.1.B.). 
  • Develop the needed skills to be successful in honors, AP, and college-level courses in the future (3.2.B.). 
  • Plan and execute service activities, projects, and presentations that will impact their school, community, or city throughout the school year (5.2.C.). 
  • Report on explicit and inferred characteristics, patterns, or behavior (WIDA ELD-SI.4-12.Inform). 
  • Support opinions with reasons and information (WIDA ELD-LA.4-5.Argue.Expressive).
  Vocabulary
Community Citizenship
  Competencies and Skills
21st Century Skills Skills for Learning and Life
Collaboration, Communication, Information Literacy, Leadership, Initiative, Productivity, Social Skills Self-Awareness, Self-Management, Social Awareness, Relationship Skills, Responsible Decision-Making
  Lesson Materials 
R.04 Slide Deck R.04 Community Posters/butcher paper  Optional: magazines, scissors, and glue for posters

Good Citizenship R.04 Slide Deck
Review objectives of the lesson with students (slide #5)
As students take their seats Students will respond to the prompt in their journal / daily worksheet. Prompt suggestions:
  • What is a legacy?
  • How does LIA help create opportunities?
Provide 5-7 minutes for students to write their reflections. Display a timer on the board if able.  OPTIONAL: Ask students to share reflections. They can pair-share, group-share in tables, or volunteer responses to the class.  For virtual class: 
  • Allow students to use the chat, a discussion board, or unmute their microphones to share responses with the class.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner column_margin="default" column_direction="default" column_direction_tablet="default" column_direction_phone="default" text_align="left" row_position="default" row_position_tablet="inherit" row_position_phone="inherit" overflow="visible" pointer_events="all"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_tablet="inherit" column_padding_phone="inherit" column_padding_position="all" column_element_direction_desktop="default" column_element_spacing="default" desktop_text_alignment="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_backdrop_filter="none" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" overflow="visible" gradient_direction="left_to_right" overlay_strength="0.3" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" animation_type="default" bg_image_animation="none" border_type="simple" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]
Lesson steps
  • (I do) Show students the video on slide #6. There are alternate video options in the slide notes. 
  • (We Do) Students will brainstorm communities they belong to. After a few minutes, ask students to share their responses  (slide #7). ADAPTATION: students can brainstorm their ideas in a journal. 
  • (You Do) Distribute R.04 Community. (slide #8). Ask students to select 3 of the communities they belong to. Then, they will brainstorm ideas for improving and contributing to each community. 
Reflection: WHAT? | SO WHAT? | NOW WHAT? (slide #9) Initiate reflection using the questions below. Students can reflect quietly or in writing before sharing out in pairs, as a group, or as a class. 
  • What? What were your thoughts and feelings as you participated in this activity?
  • So what? Why do you think it’s important to contribute to your community?
  • Now what? What will you do with what you learned about community today?
Lesson steps
  • (I Do) Show Good Citizen video on slide #10.
  • (We Do) Activate students’ prior learning by asking them to recall some of the responsibilities they have according to the CIRCLES OF RESPONSIBILITY (slide #11). 
  • (You Do) Students will work in small groups to create a poster, collage, or comic strip depicting good citizenship.
EXTENSION: present it to the class. EXTENSION: create a skit.  Virtual Class Adaptations:  
  • Conduct the lesson on an established LMS or use tools such as FlipGrid, Canvas, Miro, Google Classroom, or other interactive platform. 
  • Create a padlet and allow students to type their reflections into the padlet. 
  • Invite students to use the chat option to share their responses.

Exit ticket: Students complete one of the following prompts
  1. What can you do to be a good citizen?
  2. How does citizenship align with LIA values? 
In Person Class Assessment Options:
  • Write responses on a sticky note and place in a designated space in the classroom. 
  • Write in a journal / daily worksheet. 
  • Share out loud/with their groups
Virtual Class Assessment Options:
  • Discussion assignment on LMS.
  • Virtual board such as jamboard, miro, Zoom Whiteboard, etc.
  • Create a video on Flipgrid or Canvas.

ADAPTATIONS

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner column_margin="default" column_direction="default" column_direction_tablet="default" column_direction_phone="default" bottom_padding="7px" text_align="left" row_position="default" row_position_tablet="inherit" row_position_phone="inherit" overflow="visible" pointer_events="all"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_tablet="inherit" column_padding_phone="inherit" column_padding_position="all" column_element_direction_desktop="default" column_element_spacing="default" desktop_text_alignment="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_backdrop_filter="none" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" overflow="visible" gradient_direction="left_to_right" overlay_strength="0.3" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" animation_type="default" bg_image_animation="none" border_type="simple" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]
DIFFERENTIATION: 
  • Use sentence stems to guide student conversations. 
  • Have students write their responses to each question in a journal or worksheet before sharing out loud. 
EXTENSION: 
  • Conduct research or read Luis Fonsi’s history. https://www.biography.com/musicians/luis-fonsi 
  • Vocabulary support. Students enhance vocabulary by using a search engine or thesaurus to find synonyms for their descriptive words. 
  • Conduct a Socratic Seminar or small group discussions on the following prompts. There are no right or wrong answers, and it is important to provide a safe space for students to answer honestly.  
    • What does good citizenship mean to you? 
    • How does having good citizenship contribute to the community?
    • How can good citizenship on one person’s behalf be interpreted as bad citizenship on someone else’s behalf? 
    • Are there different cultural perspectives on what is considered good or bad citizenship?

OPTIONAL: Lead students in a midline crossing activity. Use Educational Kinesiology document to find useful resources.    45-90 minute lesson   OBJECTIVES: Students will
  • Research current events that have a direct impact on their school, local, state, and national communities (1.2.A.). 
  • Build a reciprocal support network that includes community leaders and local businesses (1.2.B.)
  • Demonstrate leadership skills (2.2.B.). 
  • Practice and use action plans to define problems, brainstorm solutions, then form and implement plans to address them (2.3.A.).
  • Plan and execute service activities, projects, and presentations that will impact their school, community, or city throughout the school year (5.2.C.). 
  • Introduce and develop a topic clearly; state an opinion (WIDA ELD-LA.4-5.Argue. Expressive).

Service Learning

21st Century Skills Skills for Learning and Life
Critical Thinking, Creativity, Collaboration, Communication, Flexibility, Leadership, Initiative, Productivity Self-Management, Social Awareness, Responsible Decision-Making

Service Learning R.05 Slide Deck 
Review objectives of the lesson with students (slide #5)
As students take their seats Students will respond to the prompt in their journal / daily worksheet. Prompt suggestions:
  • Do you agree or disagree with the quote? Explain your answer. 
  • What is an example of people doing small things that can change the world? 
Provide 5-7 minutes for students to write their reflections. Display a timer on the board if able.  OPTIONAL: Ask students to share reflections. They can pair-share, group-share in tables, or volunteer responses to the class.  For virtual class: 
  • Allow students to use the chat, a discussion board, or unmute their microphones to share responses with the class.

Lesson steps
  • (I do) Ask students what service learning is. They should already have prior knowledge from unit 1. Show students the video on slide #6. There are alternate video options in the slide notes. 
  • (We Do) Ask students to recall what they learned from the video and previous lesson. Guiding questions: What is service learning? How does it relate to citizenship?  (slide #7). ADAPTATION: students can brainstorm their ideas in a journal or small groups before sharing out with the class. 
  • (You Do) Divide students into small groups and explain that they will brainstorm service learning activities (slide #8). Distribute R.05 Service Learning. After time has elapsed, students will share their ideas with the rest of the class. 
Reflection: WHAT? | SO WHAT? | NOW WHAT? (slide #9) Initiate reflection using the questions below. Students can reflect quietly or in writing before sharing out in pairs, as a group, or as a class. 
  • What? What were your thoughts and feelings as you participated in this activity?
  • So what? Why do you think it’s important to brainstorm ideas for improving your community?
  • Now what? What will you do with what you learned about service learning today?
Lesson steps
  • In the same groups as before, students will vote on a top service learning idea from the class or from their own brainstorms. They will complete the Service Learning Proposal Form. ADAPTATION: show a pre-filled proposal form. 
Virtual Class Adaptations:  
  • Conduct the lesson on an established LMS or use tools such as FlipGrid, Canvas, Miro, Google Classroom, or other interactive platform. 
  • Create a padlet and allow students to type their reflections into the padlet. 
  • Invite students to use the chat option to share their responses.

Exit ticket: Students complete one of the following prompts
  1. Why did you select the service-learning project you selected?
  2. Do you foresee any challenges with your selected service learning activity? 
In Person Class Assessment Options:
  • Write responses on a sticky note and place in a designated space in the classroom. 
  • Write in a journal / daily worksheet. 
  • Share out loud/with their groups
Virtual Class Assessment Options:
  • Discussion assignment on LMS.
  • Virtual board such as jamboard, miro, Zoom Whiteboard, etc.
  • Create a video on Flipgrid or Canvas.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner column_margin="default" column_direction="default" column_direction_tablet="default" column_direction_phone="default" bottom_padding="7px" text_align="left" row_position="default" row_position_tablet="inherit" row_position_phone="inherit" overflow="visible" pointer_events="all"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_tablet="inherit" column_padding_phone="inherit" column_padding_position="all" column_element_direction_desktop="default" column_element_spacing="default" desktop_text_alignment="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_backdrop_filter="none" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" overflow="visible" gradient_direction="left_to_right" overlay_strength="0.3" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" animation_type="default" bg_image_animation="none" border_type="simple" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]
DIFFERENTIATION: 
  • Use sentence stems to guide student conversations. 
  • Have students write their responses to each question in a journal or worksheet before sharing out loud. 
EXTENSION: 
  • Conduct research or read Eduardo Galeano’s history. https://lannan.org/bios/eduardo-galeano 
  • Have students share their service learning proposal and as a class, vote on the top one to be the class service.

(self-awareness, social awareness, self-management, social management, social engagement) LIA Themes: Professionalism, Responsive Conflict Resolution   Setting the Stage Display the quote on the board and have students respond to one of the prompts as they get in their seats.    OPTIONAL: Play culturally relevant music as students enter the class. OPTIONAL: Lead students in a midline crossing activity. Use Educational Kinesiology document to find useful resources.    45-90 minute lesson   OBJECTIVES: Students will
  • Develop skills to aid in communication between parents, teachers, student body, and administration. 
  • Develop and enhance their linguistic proficiency (2.1).
  • Demonstrate effective and appropriate communication skills across different mediums. (2.2.A.)
  • Demonstrate leadership skills (2.2.B.).
  • Demonstrate an understanding of professional dress, appropriate behavior, and language across a variety of settings (3.1.A.). 
  • Increase interpersonal skills through interactive games and situational practice (5.2.A.)
  • Report on explicit and inferred characteristics, patterns, or behavior (WIDA ELD-SI.4-12.Inform).
  • Offer alternatives to extend or deepen awareness of factors that  contribute to particular outcomes (WIDA ELD-SI.4-12.Explain).
  • Support or challenge an opinion, premise, or interpretation (WIDA ELD-SI.4-12.Argue).
  • Support opinions with reasons and information (WIDA ELD-LA.4-5.Argue.Expressive).
  • Use a formal style (WIDA ELD-LA.4-5.Argue Expressive).
  Vocabulary
Language Register
  Competencies and Skills
21st Century Skills Skills for Learning and Life
Critical Thinking, Collaboration Communication Skills, Social Responsibility, Collaboration, Flexibility, Leadership, Social Skills Self-Awareness, Self-Management, Social Awareness, Social Engagement

Communication R.06 Slide Deck
Review objectives of the lesson with students (slide #5)
As students take their seats Students will respond to the prompt in their journal / daily worksheet. Prompt suggestions:
  • Do you need to grab onto all opportunities? Why or why not?
  • Name a time you seized an opportunity and how it has benefited you. 
Provide 5-7 minutes for students to write their reflections. Display a timer on the board if able.  OPTIONAL: Ask students to share reflections. They can pair-share, group-share in tables, or volunteer responses to the class.  For virtual class: 
  • Allow students to use the chat, a discussion board, or unmute their microphones to share responses with the class.

Lesson steps
  • (I do) Define Language Register and read the language register types to students (slide #6). ADAPTATION: print out the slide
  • (We Do) Students read the practice scenarios and share their answers.  (slide #7-#8). ADAPTATION: Four Corners Activity. 
Reflection: WHAT? | SO WHAT? | NOW WHAT? (slide #9) Initiate reflection using the questions below. Students can reflect quietly or in writing before sharing out in pairs, as a group, or as a class. 
  • What? What were your thoughts and feelings as you participated in this activity?
  • So what? Why do you think it’s important to learn about language registers?
  • Now what? What will you do with what you learned about communication today?
Lesson closure 
  • (You Do) Students will be placed in small groups and create short skits using the prompts found on slide #10 & the Group Scenarios handout. 
EXTENSION: group will explain their characters and why they chose the language register.  EXTENSION: students engage in discussion on improper language registers to use, or come up with examples. Virtual Class Adaptations:  
  • Conduct the lesson on an established LMS or use tools such as FlipGrid, Canvas, Miro, Google Classroom, or other interactive platform. 
  • Create a padlet and allow students to type their reflections into the padlet. 
  • Invite students to use the chat option to share their responses.

Exit ticket: Students complete one of the following prompts
  1. What is your takeaway about language registers?
  2. Do you think language register matters? Explain why or why not.

  • Write responses on a sticky note and place in a designated space in the classroom. 
  • Write in a journal / daily worksheet. 
  • Share out loud/with their groups

  • Create a padlet and allow students to type their reflections into the padlet.

DIFFERENTIATION: 
  • Use sentence stems to guide student conversations. 
  • Have students write their responses to each question in a journal or worksheet before sharing out loud. 
EXTENSION: 
  • Conduct research or read Celia Cruz’s history. https://www.britannica.com/biography/Celia-Cruz 
  • Vocabulary support. Students enhance vocabulary by using a search engine or thesaurus to find synonyms for their descriptive words. 
  • Students look up the lyrics to a song, and rewrite the song using a formal register. 
  • Students look up a famous presidential / other speech and rewrite it in a different register.

(self-awareness, social awareness, self-management, social management, social engagement, responsible decision-making) LIA Themes: Leadership, Professionalism   Setting the Stage Display the quote on the board and have students respond to one of the prompts as they get in their seats.    OPTIONAL: Play culturally relevant music as students enter the class. OPTIONAL: Lead students in a midline crossing activity. Use Educational Kinesiology document to find useful resources.    45-90 minute lesson   OBJECTIVES: Students will
  • Develop social skills to interact across a wide variety of age groups and social contexts (2.2).
  • Demonstrate effective and appropriate communication skills across different mediums (2.2.A.).
  • Demonstrate an understanding of appropriate behavior and language across a variety of settings (3.1.A.).
  • Increase interpersonal skills through interactive games and situational practice (5.2.A.)
  • Identify and raise questions about what might be unexplained, missing, or unsaid (WIDA ELD-SI.4-12.Narrate).
  • Report on explicit and inferred characteristics, patterns, or behavior (WIDA ELD-SI.4-12.Inform).
  • Evaluate the impact of key word choices in a text (WIDA ELD-LA.4-5.Inform.Interpretive).
  • Use a formal style (WIDA ELD-LA.4-5.Argue.Expressive).
  Vocabulary
Communication Miscommunication Perception
  Competencies and Skills
21st Century Skills Skills for Learning and Life
Critical Thinking, Communication Skills, Media Literacy, Social Responsibility, Flexibility, Leadership, Social Skills Self-Awareness, Self-Management, Social Awareness, Social Engagement, Responsible Decision-Making

Written Communication R.07 Slide Deck
Review objectives of the lesson with students (slide #5)
As students take their seats Students will respond to the prompt in their journal / daily worksheet. Prompt suggestions:
  • How have you used writing to express yourself?
  • Do you believe writing can help fight unhappiness? Explain your answer. 
Provide 5-7 minutes for students to write their reflections. Display a timer on the board if able.  OPTIONAL: Ask students to share reflections. They can pair-share, group-share in tables, or volunteer responses to the class.  For virtual class: 
  • Allow students to use the chat, a discussion board, or unmute their microphones to share responses with the class.

LESSON

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner column_margin="default" column_direction="default" column_direction_tablet="default" column_direction_phone="default" text_align="left" row_position="default" row_position_tablet="inherit" row_position_phone="inherit" overflow="visible" pointer_events="all"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_tablet="inherit" column_padding_phone="inherit" column_padding_position="all" column_element_direction_desktop="default" column_element_spacing="default" desktop_text_alignment="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_backdrop_filter="none" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" overflow="visible" gradient_direction="left_to_right" overlay_strength="0.3" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" animation_type="default" bg_image_animation="none" border_type="simple" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]
Lesson steps [Slides #6-#8 are the same in Lessons 7 and 8. If taught during this lesson, it does not need to be taught in the other lesson]
  • Ask students to define communication and brainstorm ways we communicate (slide #6). Once you have a definition and a few examples, move on to slide #7. ADAPTATION: print out the slide so students can brainstorm in writing ADAPTATION: use the definition from the Vocabulary Slide Deck 
  • Ask students to refer back to their brainstorms and sort the communication methods in verbal and written communication. (slide #7-#8). OPTIONAL: use the Venn Diagram on slide #8 to sort communication types.  
  • On slide #9 list the written communication methods identified by students. Then, ask students to share miscommunications that can happen. EXTENSION: ask students to rank the possible miscommunications from “most miscommunications” to “least miscommunications” and have students explain the reasoning behind their rankings. 
  • Practice! Slides #10 and #11 are two email examples. Ask students the strengths and weaknesses of each email. Then ask them what can be done to enhance the communication of the email. 
  • Practice! Slides #12 and #13 are two text message examples. On slide #12, ask students what miscommunications can occur with a vague and short message. Ask if the clarity of the message changes based on who it comes from and what it is in response to. Students should explain their answers. On slide #13, students will see the same message with different punctuation. How and why is it different?
  • Practice! Slide #14 has a social media post. Ask students the questions written in the slide notes. 
Reflection: WHAT? | SO WHAT? | NOW WHAT? (slide #15) Initiate reflection using the questions below. Students can reflect quietly or in writing before sharing out in pairs, as a group, or as a class. 
  • What? What were your thoughts and feelings as you participated in this activity?
  • So what? Why do you think it’s important to know how to communicate in writing?
  • Now what? What will you do with what you learned about written communication today?
Lesson closure 
  • (You Do) Students will be placed in small groups and create short skits using the prompts found on slide #16 - #19 & the Group Scenarios handout. 
Option 1: split students into groups and have them work on one scenario per group. Option 2: split students into groups and have them work on each of the scenarios.  Option 3: students work through each of the scenarios individually. 
  • After working through the scenarios, students will share their responses with the class and get feedback from each other. 
Virtual Class Adaptations:  
  • Conduct the lesson on an established LMS or use tools such as FlipGrid, Canvas, Miro, Google Classroom, or other interactive platform. 
  • Create a padlet and allow students to type their reflections into the padlet. 
  • Invite students to use the chat option to share their responses. 
Note: Teachers may adapt the content to best suit their classroom. [/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner column_margin="default" column_direction="default" column_direction_tablet="default" column_direction_phone="default" text_align="left" row_position="default" row_position_tablet="inherit" row_position_phone="inherit" overflow="visible" pointer_events="all"][vc_column_inner column_padding="padding-5-percent" column_padding_tablet="inherit" column_padding_phone="inherit" column_padding_position="all" column_element_direction_desktop="default" column_element_spacing="default" desktop_text_alignment="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" background_color="#3a3a3a" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_backdrop_filter="none" font_color="#ffffff" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" overflow="visible" gradient_direction="left_to_right" overlay_strength="0.3" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" animation_type="default" bg_image_animation="none" border_type="simple" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text]

Exit ticket: Students complete one of the following prompts
  1. What does it mean to be intentional in written communication?
  2. How does your written communication reflect responsibility?
In Person Class Assessment Options:
  • Write responses on a sticky note and place in a designated space in the classroom. 
  • Write in a journal / daily worksheet. 
  • Share out loud/with their groups
Virtual Class Assessment Options:
  • Discussion assignment on LMS.
  • Virtual board such as jamboard, miro, Zoom Whiteboard, etc.
  • Create a video on Flipgrid or Canvas.

ADAPTATIONS

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner column_margin="default" column_direction="default" column_direction_tablet="default" column_direction_phone="default" bottom_padding="7px" text_align="left" row_position="default" row_position_tablet="inherit" row_position_phone="inherit" overflow="visible" pointer_events="all"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_tablet="inherit" column_padding_phone="inherit" column_padding_position="all" column_element_direction_desktop="default" column_element_spacing="default" desktop_text_alignment="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_backdrop_filter="none" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" overflow="visible" gradient_direction="left_to_right" overlay_strength="0.3" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" animation_type="default" bg_image_animation="none" border_type="simple" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]
DIFFERENTIATION: 
  • Use sentence stems to guide student conversations. 
  • Have students write their responses to each question in a journal or worksheet before sharing out loud. 
EXTENSION: 
  • Conduct research or read Mario Vargas Llosas’s history. https://www.britannica.com/biography/Mario-Vargas-Llosa 
  • Vocabulary support. Students enhance vocabulary by using a search engine or thesaurus to find synonyms for their descriptive words. 
  • Have students come up with their own examples of written communication.

(self-awareness, social awareness, self-management, social management, social engagement) LIA Themes: Academic Excellence, Leadership, Professionalism, Responsive Conflict Resolution   Setting the Stage Display the quote on the board and have students respond to one of the prompts as they get in their seats.    OPTIONAL: Play culturally relevant music as students enter the class. OPTIONAL: Lead students in a midline crossing activity. Use Educational Kinesiology document to find useful resources.    45-90 minute lesson   OBJECTIVES: Students will
  • Read, write, and speak academically in both languages (2.1.A.)
  • Develop social skills to interact across a wide variety of age groups and social contexts (2.2).
  • Demonstrate effective and appropriate communication skills across different mediums (2.2.A.).
  • Demonstrate an understanding of appropriate behavior and language across a variety of settings (3.1.A.).
  • Increase interpersonal skills through interactive games and situational practice (5.2.A.)
  • Use a formal style (WIDA ELD-LA.4-5.Argue.Expressive).

Written Communication R.08 Slide Deck
Review objectives of the lesson with students (slide #5)
As students take their seats Students will respond to the prompt in their journal / daily worksheet. Prompt suggestions:
  • How does LIA prepare youth to be change agents in their societies?
  • What have you learned about being a change agent?
Provide 5-7 minutes for students to write their reflections. Display a timer on the board if able.  OPTIONAL: Ask students to share reflections. They can pair-share, group-share in tables, or volunteer responses to the class.  For virtual class: 
  • Allow students to use the chat, a discussion board, or unmute their microphones to share responses with the class.
